record.title: 65th Sakura Matsuri – Japanese Street Festival
record.address: Pennsylvania Avenue, NW - Between 3rd and 7th Streets, Washington, DC 20001
record.description: Prepare your senses for an extraordinary cultural journey at the 65th Sakura Matsuri – Japanese Street Festival on April 10th–11th, 2027 from 10:30 a.m. Saturday through 4:00 p.m. Sunday at Pennsylvania & Constitution Avenues, 3rd–7th Street NW in the heart of Washington, D.C. Presented by Japan-America Society of Washington DC, this Premier Event of the National Cherry Blossom Festival is an immersive celebration of Japanese tradition, artistry, and spirit that will transport you across the Pacific without leaving the nation’s capital. Lose yourself in the vibrant pulse of authentic Japanese culture. Watch as traditional and contemporary performances unfold on multiple stages—dance, music, and theatrical magic that capture the essence of Japan’s rich heritage. Your palate will sing as you savor exquisite Japanese cuisine from vendors offering everything from street food favorites to culinary masterpieces. Browse captivating exhibits that showcase Japanese art, craftsmanship, and cultural treasures. Encounter roaming performers, artisans demonstrating time-honored techniques, and interactive experiences that invite you to participate in the celebration. This isn’t just a festival—it’s a cultural gateway, a two-day immersion that honors the profound friendship between Japan and America, symbolized by the cherry blossoms themselves. Whether you’re discovering Japanese culture for the first time or returning as a devoted enthusiast, Sakura Matsuri welcomes you with open arms and authentic spirit. Tickets go on sale in late fall 2026. Easily accessible via Metro. 65th Sakura Matsuri – Japanese Street Festival is where tradition meets community, where cherry blossoms bloom as a bridge between nations. record.title: A Not-So-Silent Night
record.description: Jammin' Java presents "A Not-So-Silent Night," a lively holiday-themed show on Wednesday, December 3rd, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. This festive celebration features three accomplished artists—Mama's Black Sheep, Regina Sayles, and Colleen Clark—performing original songs alongside holiday favorites to get audiences in the spirit of the season. The show brims with sing-along opportunities and welcomes all ages, from kids to grandparents, making it a joyful holiday event for the whole family. Mama's Black Sheep is the soulful collaboration of singer-songwriters Ashland Miller (guitar/vocals) and Laura Cerulli (drums/vocals), creating a blend of hit-worthy originals and covers with a unique spin spanning country, pop, soul, and blues. The duo has been making music and touring extensively for over 15 years, with five well-received albums including their newest release "Fight Back With Love" (October 2024). Regina Sayles, based in East Stroudsburg, PA, performs 100+ live shows annually, playing original music and a wide variety of covers across all genres. She's a featured vocalist in the Craig Thatcher Band and recently joined forces with Mama's Black Sheep on bass and vocals. Regina has appeared with folk pioneer Tret Fure and feminist icon Ani DiFranco, and her former duo Porter & Sayles was featured on the Melissa Etheridge Cruise. Colleen Clark, a musician and audio engineer from Rehoboth Beach, DE, has performed with Christine Havrilla & Gypsy Fuzz, Mama's Black Sheep, Red Letter Day, and others, while serving as Associate Professor in the Music Program at Salisbury University teaching audio production, live sound engineering, acoustics, and ear training. "A Not-So-Silent Night" combines heartfelt musicianship, holiday cheer, and authentic artistry in Fairfax County, Virginia. Tickets start at $40. record.title: Adam Ezra Group
record.description: Jammin' Java welcomes Adam Ezra Group on Thursday, November 14th, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. Over more than two decades of relentless grassroots touring, Adam Ezra Group has built something far bigger than a typical touring band: a fiercely independent, fan-powered community that expands one show at a time. Rooms across the country sell out when Adam Ezra Group comes to town, with longtime fans regularly traveling across state lines to catch multiple shows, drawn by the band's deep sense of community and the promise that no two nights are ever the same. The band never performs from a fixed setlist; instead, they shape each night around the energy in the room. Songs, stories, and moments unfold in real time—part concert, part revival, and part reminder of what live music can still be at its best. Blending folk/Americana soul, rock 'n' roll energy, and deeply human songwriting, Adam Ezra Group has built one of the most authentic underground followings in live music today while quickly becoming recognized on a national level. SPIN describes them as "an independent underground folk band blowing up without selling out," a rise powered entirely by word of mouth, community activism, and genuine connection between band and audience that turns first-time listeners into lifelong fans. Catch them now while they're still playing intimate rooms where you can give Adam a hug on your way out. Adam Ezra Group delivers authentic artistry, community spirit, and unforgettable live music in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: African American Quilt Documentation Day in DC
record.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts - Great Hall
record.address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005-3970
record.description: WASHINGTON, DC — The African American Quilt Documentation Study Group (AAQDSG) will host a FREE quilt documentation event in Washington, DC on Sunday, November 1, 2026, inviting the African American community to bring family quilts in to be documented, preserved, and honored as part of our shared history. Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005 Cost: Free — pre-registration required (time slots are limited) Since the 1980s, quilt documentation has been used to preserve family legacies and record the social, cultural, and artistic significance of quilts. African American family quilts have historically been excluded from this process. Most exist today with no documented history of the quilt or its maker — what's known has been passed down orally and never recorded. "Documentation is how we hold onto that," said A'donna Richardson, Director of AAQDSG. "It's an act of honoring our ancestors, of making sure the work of the quilt maker's hands is remembered. It's a way of saying: our ancestors mattered, what they made matters, and the stories tied to their quilts matter." The process reaches beyond individual families. Documented quilts become part of the historical record that scholars, museums, and researchers rely on to understand African American creativity, survival, faith, and community. Without this work, those stories remain untold and the historical record remains misrepresented and incomplete. We are encouraging the African American community to bring their family quilts, in whatever condition (the older, the better), to the November 1 event to have them photographed and documented, and to share the stories behind them. YOU MUST REGISTER to attend: https://aaqdsg.org/events If all appointment slots are filled, send your name and contact information to afamquilydoc@aadqsg.org. Contact: A'donna Richardson, Director, AAQDSG Website: https://aaqdsg.org Email:

record.description: Old Glory, reimagined: artists transform our flag over the centuries. Across generations, the Stars and Stripes has inspired pride, protest, and profound artistic expression. record.title: An Evening with Caleb Caudle & The Sweet Critters
record.description: Caleb Caudle, a North Carolina native, has built his artistry through endurance and steady momentum, carrying him from small foothills stages to the Grand Ole Opry. Now he enters a pivotal chapter—one where life and art converge powerfully. The discovery that he and his wife are expecting their first child has added new perspective to his artistic vision. On his new album Heavy Thrill, recorded at the storied Cash Cabin in Hendersonville, Tennessee, Caudle self-produces for the first time, embracing what he calls "the patina of life." "Our plans rarely shake out the way we want them to," he says. "This record is about doing the most with what you're given and weathering the storms." With this release, Caudle launches his own label, Handplow Records, named after a rusty red steel handplow used for generations of tobacco farming by his family—a symbol of toil, dedication, and the sweetness that yields from hard work. Heavy Thrill, mixed by Jacquire King (Tom Waits, Modest Mouse) and mastered by Pete Lyman (Chris Stapleton, John Prine), captures life as it leaves its mark through intimate portraits of flawed, deeply human lives. Rolling Stone calls his music "the musical equivalent of high-proof bourbon—rich in flavor, with a subtle, satisfying bite." His critically acclaimed career spans Merlefest, Luck Reunion, and Kerrville Folk Festival, with praise from The New York Times, NPR, and No Depression. Jammin' Java welcomes this artist to near Fairfax County, Virginia.

record.title: An Evening with Mike Dawes
record.description: Mike Dawes, an English fingerstyle guitarist, composes, arranges, and performs multiple parts simultaneously on a single guitar: a mastery that earned him 'Best Acoustic Guitarist in the World' from Total Guitar Magazine and MusicRadar reader polls in 2017 and 2018. Regarded as one of the world's most creative modern fingerstyle guitarists, Dawes performs alongside Justin Hayward of The Moody Blues and has earned praise from YouTube personality Rick Beato as "one of the finest acoustic guitar players in the world." His viral debut arrangement of Gotye's "Somebody That I Used to Know" garnered tens of millions of YouTube views, a success he's duplicated with arrangements of "One," "The Impossible," and "Jump" across multiple platforms. His reputation has invited collaborations with Grammy Award-winning artists including Tommy Emmanuel on the duet record Accomplice Vol. Expect a masterclass in solo guitar virtuosity one musician creating the illusion of an ensemble through technical precision, musicality, and creative arrangement. Jammin' Java welcomes this innovative guitarist to near Fairfax County, Virginia.

record.title: An Evening with Trace Bundy
record.description: Internationally-acclaimed guitar virtuoso Trace Bundy must be seen, not just heard. His music is poetry in motion, using harmonics, looping, multiple capos, and his unique banter and stage presence to deliver an unforgettable live concert experience. Listening to his intricate arrangements is one thing, but seeing the fan-dubbed “Acoustic Ninja” play live confounds even the most accomplished music lovers as to how one person can do all that with just two hands and ten fingers. Bundy’s unique career has brought him across the world, with concerts in 28 countries and counting – from high-tech performance halls in South Korea and Italy, to remote villages in Zimbabwe and Guatemala. He has independently sold over 150,000 albums on his record label, Honest Ninja Music. His video clips circulate virally at astonishing speed, with over 45 million YouTube views to date.​ Jimmy Leslie at Guitar Player Magazine blogs “It was easy to see why Bundy plays bigger venues on each tour. In his hands, the acoustic guitar is an imagination station, and there was no telling where he is going take the audience at any given turn. Thrilling stuff.”​ Audiocast Magazine from Austin, TX agrees: “Bundy’s live show is without a doubt an event that needs to be witnessed rather than told about. With such a jaw-dropping performance, Bundy’s live concert is a slap in the face that would leave a palm print on the memory of everyone in the audience.” Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Baby Bugs
record.description: Baby Bugs is an alternative music project founded by Bowie. Raised on bluegrass guitar and church hymns, Bowie spent years held under the weight of religious trauma and emotional abuse before discovering that writing their feelings in the form of a song or poem was the only way to express themselves clearly. In 2021 at the age of 18, Bowie released their first song "Hey Bunny". Surpassing 2 million streams in its first 60 days and receiving an outpour from fans encouraging Baby Bugs for more, Bowie decided to continue to write and record songs with the goal to help others who have experienced similar hardships feel less alone.

Expect campy humor, a killer score, and a wild ride from start to finish! Inspired on a ridiculous tabloid story from the pages of the legendary Weekly World News, Bat Boy: The Musical is a comedy/horror show about a half-boy/half-bat creature who is discovered in a cave near Hope Falls, West Virginia. For lack of a better solution, the local sheriff brings Bat Boy to the home of the town veterinarian, Dr. Parker, where he is eventually accepted as a member of the family and taught to act like a “normal” boy by the veterinarian’s wife, Meredith, and teenage daughter, Shelley. Bat Boy is happy with his new life, but when he naively tries to fit in with the narrow-minded people of Hope Falls, trouble begins! You don’t need to be a fan of the original urban legend to love this show. If you like comedy mixed with a bit of horror and rock music, welcome to Hope Falls! You don’t even need to be a fan of musicals to love this show. As long as you like having fun… this show is for you. Is it scary? No! Is it gory ? No! ... well, maybe a tiny bit. record.title: Bison: Standing Strong

record.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

record.title: Bronze Bison: Exhibit
record.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
record.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. The original bison diorama introduced generations of visitors to an animal and a prairie landscape they had never seen and helped spark the bison conservation movement. The new bison bronzes will welcome visitors from around the world and celebrate America’s national mammal. Gift of Naoma Tate and the family of Hal Tate.

record.description: CHARLIE BERENS is Wisconsin’s most popular stand-up comedian and he's best known for creating feel-good, Midwest focused comedy like his popular local news series “The Manitowoc Minute,” his two specials, and podcasts, “Bellied Up” and “The Cripescast” which have garnered 12M+ FOLLOWERS and 3B+ VIEWS. He’s the New York Times Best-Selling Author of "The Midwest Survival Guide," an Emmy-winning journalist, and a Billboard-topping bluegrass musician. Charlie’s many things to many people, but at his core, his comedy comes from growing up in a big family - he’s one of twelve – taking pride in being a DIY-er, ice fishing and gambling with his grandma. While grounded in Midwest culture, Charlie’s stand up tours consistently land on a national level, selling over 400K tickets in 113 cities in 32 states and included 9 ARENA SHOWS in the past 4 years. He works with many of Wisconsin's homegrown brands, charities, and sports teams and he reaches people most comedians don’t — heavily rural, spanning multiple generations, and straddling both sides of the political spectrum. He has been the face of Wisconsin’s Annual Food for the Holidays Campaign for the past four years and lately, he’s been advocating for Wisconsinites against A.I. data centers and found himself squaring off with tech giants and politicians like a modern-day Erin Brockovich. Wisconsin gave Charlie a voice and now he's giving back. record.title: Charlie Parr
record.description: Charlie Parr, a Duluth-based guitarist and folk troubadour, delivers what Rolling Stone calls "a gritty blend of Delta blues and Depression-era roots music soaked in his hardscrabble voice," and NPR praises as "expertly picked resonator guitar and lyrics that puncture the soul." Over two-and-a-half decades, Parr has released twenty albums while performing up to 275 shows a year at tastemaker events like Newport Folk Fest and Pickathon. A continuer of folk tradition, Parr's sound draws from Folkways legends like Lead Belly and Woody Guthrie, imbued with blues and folk echoes of decades past. His music is shaped by his working-class Minnesota upbringing and Depression-era stories from his father. His 2021 Smithsonian Folkways debut Last of the Better Days Ahead foregrounded his lyrical craftsmanship and bluesman confidence with spare production elevating his blues poetry. His 2024 release Little Sun wove together stories celebrating music, community, and nature into an ambitious, raw album exemplifying his blend of blues and folk traditions with poetic originality. His 2026 album Rooming House joins the chorus of WPA-era socially conscious folk operas and outlaw country concept albums, poignantly allegorizing his experiences and those around him. Jammin' Java welcomes him to Fairfax County, Virginia.

record.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. record.title: Credit Union Cherry Blossom 10 Mile
record.description: Lace up your running shoes and join thousands of passionate runners at the Credit Union Cherry Blossom 10 Mile Run on Sunday, April 4th, 2027 at Washington Monument Grounds in Washington, D.C. This iconic race kicks off with the Elite Women’s Start at 7:18 a.m., followed by the full 10 Mile Start at 7:30 a.m., creating an electric morning of speed, determination, and spring celebration. Run through the heart of the nation’s capital while surrounded by the ethereal beauty of blooming cherry blossoms—a truly unforgettable racing experience. Race Registration Options: The fields for the 2027 10 Mile, 5K, and Double Blossom (run the 5K on Saturday, April 3 and the 10 Mile on Sunday, April 4) are determined by lottery. The Lottery opens at 10:00 a.m. on December 14th, 2026 and closes at midnight on January 5th, 2027. Beyond the lottery, multiple pathways to entry exist: 100 Mile Club: Members who have completed at least 100 miles in any combination of the 10 Mile or 5K races can gain guaranteed entry. Check your status in the All-Time Results Database (1973–2026). Two-Time Loser Entries: Runners who entered the lottery in 2025 and 2026 without success qualify for a separate TTL registration process. Charity Entries: Miss the lottery? Raise $500 for Children’s Miracle Network and secure your spot as a Charity Race Entry Participant. Every dollar supports 170 non-profit children’s hospitals across North America. Seeded Runners: Top open and age-group runners can request special seeded status (deadline: February 15th, 2027) and start in the Yellow Corral immediately behind elite athletes. Volunteers: Give back and get guaranteed entry into next year’s race—a transferable benefit that makes volunteering the gift that keeps giving. Credit Union Cherry Blossom 10 Mile Run combines athletic excellence, community spirit, charitable giving, and the incomparable beauty of spring in the nation’s capital. Join your community for dinner from 5:00–5:30 p.m.; the author lecture begins at 6:00 p.m. Dragon Falls isn't just a thriller—it's an insider's view of how cyber warfare and high-tech attacks are currently threatening our world. Retired Navy Commander Jack Tanner arrives in Malaysia on a cybersecurity book tour only to discover that Beijing's shadow war is far more sophisticated than anyone imagined. The Chinese Ministry of State Security and their cyber operatives, known as the Three Immortals, orchestrate a devastating espionage campaign combining intelligence, financial manipulation, autonomous drone swarms, and jungle-based insurgents to destabilize Southeast Asia's strongest democracy. Dragon Falls delivers the complexity of Ludlum-inspired spy conspiracies with Clancy-style techno-thriller sophistication, revealing how today's real technologies are reshaping global conflict. This is the warfare we must master if our way of life is to endure. Brad Meltzer, bestselling author of The Viper, calls it "terrifying and utterly authentic." Shyam Sankar, CTO of Palantir, praises it as "a rare thriller that actually understands the battlefield" with tradecraft that is "real, sequences spot on, and stakes exactly where they should be: on America's need to understand Beijing's shadow war." Bob Gourley, the author, brings expertise from his career in cybersecurity and national security affairs, offering authentic insights into modern espionage and cyber warfare. Meet the author, purchase Dragon Falls, and have it signed following the lecture. Dragon Falls: Agentic AI and Book Signing combines thrilling storytelling, national security education, and community connection in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Entertainment Nation
record.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
record.description: Entertainment has the power to captivate, inspire and transform us. It brings us together. We share it when we spontaneously recite lines from a favorite movie, dance to the same groove or recreate a national sports moment on a neighborhood street. It can also spur critical conversations, expose divides, and foster important historical change. Through the National Museum of American History’s extraordinary collection of theater, music, sports, movie and television objects, the exhibition features a powerful, ever-changing selection of objects and interactive experiences. Through the objects and their stories, the exhibition explores how, for more than 150 years, entertainment has provided a forum for important national conversations about who we are, and who we want to be.

record.description: For fans of We The Kingdom, Jamie MacDonald, and CAIN Franni Cash doesn’t just say what’s on her mind; she sings it as loudly as possible. The GRAMMY® Award-nominated Platinum singer, songwriter, and producer isn’t afraid to speak truth to power, tear down false idols, or point out hypocrisy when it comes to religion, church, or “Country Club Christians” —as she does on the likes of “Church Clothes” and “Koolaid. ” Opening up about her doubts, questions, and struggles in conversation, at shows, and on tape has made her faith stronger and given her music meaning. To paint a personal picture, she chooses to sonically color outside of the lines. The songstress spikes soulful-style hooks with rock ‘n’ roll attitude, bringing soul to Americana-style instrumentation, as she laces a sly sense of humor into the fabric of her unapologetic storytelling. She even co-opts and reclaims words and phrases once used to lambast her (such as “Jezebel”) for her own. Now, Franni declares who she is on her 2026 debut LP , Here I Am. She intentionally arranged and sequenced this 13-track body of work to tell her story in the order that she wanted to. Over the course of the journey, she looked back on how far she’s come. “I don’t know anybody who hasn’t had a problem with religion at some point, ” she observes. “Just because you’ve been burned by a church or by broken people in the church, it doesn’t mean you can’t have faith. To me, that’s what this record is about. It’s about coming back to music and true faith in a relationship with God, addressing the pain and ultimately seeking to heal from it. ” Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn
record.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. On View: June 27 – December 30, 2026 Admission: Free (with suggested donation)

record.description: Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House presents Historic Grounds: Community History in Alexandria on Saturday, November 21st, 2026 from 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. at 9000 Richmond Highway in Alexandria, Fairfax County area, Virginia. This program is part of the Historic Grounds series, where scholarly research bridges with community dialogue. Each session pairs scholarly insight with discussion, offering a unique space to learn, reflect, and connect. Join Francesco De Salvatore, Director and Curator of the Alexandria Oral History Center, and descendants of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Cemetery (a historic African American burial ground) and the Colored Rosemont community (site of some of the first African American homeowners in Alexandria) as they discuss two community history initiatives being completed in Alexandria, Virginia. The afternoon unfolds as follows: 2:00 p.m. welcomes guests with subject matter expert exploration of local history and its national relevance, followed by spirited conversation over coffee and light refreshments. At 3:00 p.m., an exclusive experience tied to the day's topic offers specialized tours or vault access to rarely seen collection objects. Your ticket includes lecture and Q&A admission to the keynote presentation and interactive discussion; a copy of Freedom in the Age of Slavery: A History of Free People of Color in Virginia; vault access to rarely seen artifacts from the Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House Collection; access to the Woodlawn estate for open house tours; and complimentary coffee and light refreshments. Francesco De Salvatore is a public historian, memory worker, and archivist committed to ethical, stakeholder-driven historical preservation. They founded and direct the City of Alexandria's Alexandria Oral History Center, a community-driven collaboration documenting and preserving Alexandria's stories and memories. Francesco holds an M.A. in History from the University of Illinois at Chicago and an M.A. in American Studies from Geor

Reese, Senior Manager of Public Programs & Interpretation at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House, as she examines how loss leaves its mark on both human history and physical spaces. record.description: The Vine presents Improv Church, a unique comedy experience that gathers community for laughter, storytelling, and connection on select dates in 2026 from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. at 2501 Gallows Road in Dunn Loring, Fairfax County, Virginia. This is improv comedy that takes place in a church—literally. The pastor, an improv comedian who has performed across the country, gives the monologue that kicks off the show. Improv Church celebrates the belief that the church is the gathered people of God—all of us. Improv is about connection and telling stories while highlighting the joy, failures, and foibles of real life. The Bible is full of those stories too, creating a cool opportunity to gather and enjoy legitimate improv comedy while exploring the intersection of faith and real life in community. Laughing together is good for the church and for people with no interest in the church—just come, it's good. This is a completely improvised comedy show featuring off-color language and scenarios with no restrictions on the comedians. The human condition can be hilarious as can a well-placed word. Ages 14+. Admission is $10. Improv Church combines comedy, community, faith exploration, and authentic human connection in Fairfax County, Virginia. Contact: vine2501@gmail.com / (703) 573-5836. record.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness
record.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
record.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

record.title: Jazz 4 Justice™
record.venue: George Mason Center for the Arts, Concert Hall
record.description: Join us as we celebrate the 25th Anniversary of Jazz4Justice™, an award-winning partnership between the George Mason University Jazz Program and Northern Virginia's legal community. For a quarter century, Jazz4Justice has demonstrated the power of music to unite communities, raise awareness of the justice gap, and support access to civil legal services for those who cannot afford an attorney. Recognized by the legal profession and honored with George Mason University's Jack Wood Award for Town-Gown Collaboration, Jazz4Justice has become a model for meaningful community engagement. In partnership with Legal Services of Northern Virginia, proceeds from this concert help provide free civil legal assistance to low-income individuals and families facing issues such as housing, domestic violence, consumer protection, family law, veterans' services, and public benefits. Through volunteer attorneys and dedicated legal advocates, LSNV works every day to help ensure that justice is not determined by one's ability to pay. The evening will feature the George Mason Jazz Program performing swinging classics from the golden age of the big band, celebrating both the enduring spirit of jazz and the remarkable partnership that has helped strengthen our community for twenty-five years. Tickets: $25 Adult, $20 Senior, $20 Youth

record.description: For fans of Eddie 9V, Nik Parr & The Selfless Lovers, and Gov't Mule Appalachian space-funk innovator Jeremy Short showcases his guitar prowess alongside blues-rock powerhouse Jared James Nichols on his new single, “ Until We’re Done ,” an explosive collaboration that finds the two guitarists trading blistering solos amidst a hazy, psychedelic soundscape of wailing guitars, soulful vocals, and hard-driving grooves. On “Until We’re Done,” Short puts his own advice into practice: make the most of the time you’re given, take the shot, and don’t let fear keep you from asking for what you want. Putting those words to the test, he reached out to one of his longtime guitar heroes with nothing more than a demo and a cold email. A fan of Nichols’ playing for nearly a decade, Short spotted his email address on the advance for a benefit concert they were both playing. He decided to reach out, sending Nichols a demo of the track along with a cold pitch explaining why he felt his bluesy hard-rock style would be a perfect fit for the track. “I didn’t expect a reply,” Short said. “I just figured, what the hell, take the shot, and whatever happens, happens.” Not long after, an email arrived from Nichols’ manager confirming that Jared connected with the song and wanted to lay down some leads. For Short, the response was surreal. “It felt like 15-year-old me would be proud of myself for taking a chance on something he believed in,” he added. “It felt like I was opening a door to a room I didn’t previously have access to, and that I had better prove myself worthy of being in the presence of the type of people who occupy that room.” Recorded at Jon Osborne’s Pine Box Studio in Nashville, “Until We’re Done’ came together under the direction of producer Justin Francis, a longtime collaborator of Short’s and fellow Whizzbang Music brother in arms. record.title: Kate Voegele "Then & Now" Tour
record.description: Singer-songwriter and One Tree Hill alum Kate Voegele returns to the stage with Then & Now, an intimate new tour built around the songs — and the stories behind them. After revisiting the music of One Tree Hill on tour last year, Voegele is digging deeper into the catalog this time, bringing back songs from her years as Mia Catalano that haven’t been heard live in years alongside music from her new album, Age of Alchemy. Built around storytelling and songwriting, Then & Now traces the unexpected threads between songs Voegele wrote at the beginning of her career and the artist she is today — how the same emotions change with time, what she understands differently now, and the stories behind the songs that she’s never shared before. Part concert, part trip through the pages of her songwriting history, Then & Now offers fans a rare chance to experience nearly two decades of Kate Voegele’s music in a completely new way: the old songs, the new songs, and everything that happened in between. record.title: Kim Richey with Special Guest Caroline Spence
record.description: Two acclaimed Nashville songwriters converge for an evening of crystalline vocals and deft artistry. Kim Richey, from her critically acclaimed 1995 self-titled debut through Long Way Back…The Songs of Glimmer in 2020, has consistently impressed listeners and attracted famous fans. She's penned No. 1 hits for Radney Foster and Trisha Yearwood—the latter earning her a Grammy nomination for Best Country Song—and written for Mary Chapin Carpenter, Patty Loveless, and Brooks and Dunn. Her voice has graced recordings from Jason Isbell's watershed Southeastern to Trisha Yearwood's Everybody Knows to Ryan Adams' Heartbreaker, providing peerless harmonies. Caroline Spence, a Nashville-based singer-songwriter, has built a devoted following across five solo albums featured by Rolling Stone, Pitchfork, and NPR. Established artists like Emmylou Harris, Matt Berninger of The National, and Sarah Jarosz have joined her as featured vocalists; her work has streamed over 80 million times. She's toured as an opening act for Tyler Childers, Mary Chapin Carpenter, and John Moreland, headlining across the US, UK, and Europe. Both artists bring the kind of songwriting precision and vocal artistry that defines Nashville's most respected voices. Jammin' Java welcomes these two powerhouses to Fairfax County, Virginia.

record.title: Leanna Firestone
record.description: Leanna Firestone is a Nashville, Tennessee based singer songwriter and multi instrumentalist known for candid, diaristic indie pop. Her songs often draw from uncomfortable memories, awkward moments, and personal experiences, pairing confessional lyrics with acoustic driven production. She began building an audience during the pandemic by sharing original music on TikTok while studying Commercial Songwriting at Middle Tennessee State University. In 2021, her song “Strawberry Mentos” gained traction on the platform, becoming the lead single of her debut EP, Y/N, which has since gained tens of millions of streams across platforms. Firestone has continued to release music steadily, including her album Forward / Slash (2022), the EPs Public Displays of Affection and Good Grief (2023), and fan-favorite single “Becoming Unbecoming” (2024). In 2025, she released her live EP An Evening with Leanna Firestone (Acoustic at The Deli) and toured with Natasha Bedingfield. Her latest album, The Answer, featuring the lead single “Victory Lap, ” was released in May 2026, followed by the first leg of her headline tour across the US and Toronto. record.description: Fabulously fun and international award-winning Legally Blonde - The Musical is the ultimate Broadway tribute to Girl Power! The story follows the transformation of Elle Woods as she tackles stereotypes, sexism, snobbery and scandal in pursuit of her dreams, and proves that you can be both legally blonde AND the smartest person in the room. This contemporary, topical story touches on many current hot-button issues while delighting audiences with memorable songs and explosive dances. Legally Blonde warms the heart by proving that self-discovery never goes out of style! Elle Woods appears to have it all. Her life is turned upside down, however, when her boyfriend dumps her so he can start getting more serious about his life and attend Harvard Law. Determined to get him back, Elle uses her brain and ingenuity to get into Harvard too. School begins with endless struggles, but with the help of her new friends, Elle quickly realizes her potential, and her true assets, as she sets out to prove herself to the world and make everyone a believer. Based on the iconic movie, Legally Blonde will take you from the sorority house to the halls of justice with Broadway’s brightest heroine and, of course, her Chihuahua, Bruiser. “A high-energy… hymn to the glories of girlishness.” – The New York Times Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Lexus Global Lacrosse Games
record.description: The Premier Lacrosse League (PLL), Women's Lacrosse League (WLL), and National Lacrosse League (NLL) unite to present the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games, a groundbreaking international competition featuring the world's best men's and women's lacrosse players representing four nations. Sanctioned by World Lacrosse and USA Lacrosse, this historic event will be played under Olympic Sixes rules—the same format competing at the LA28 Games—marking lacrosse's return to Olympic competition for the first time since 1908. For the first time ever, the PLL and NLL have collaborated to make top men's players from both leagues available to represent their countries, creating fierce national competition at the highest level. This tournament replaces the Championship Series in the PLL and WLL competition calendar for the next two years leading up to LA28, representing the next evolution in professional lacrosse's Olympic movement. Co-founded by lacrosse superstar Paul Rabil, the PLL is backed by major investors including Joe Tsai Sports and Ares, and distributed through exclusive media rights agreements with ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, and ESPN+. The NLL, North America's largest professional indoor lacrosse league, welcomed over 1 million fans during the 2025–26 season across 14 franchises. Experience elite lacrosse competition in Fairfax County, Virginia, at The St. James , a premier sports facility where you can take a 3D tour before your visit. After the games, head to one of Fairfax County's amazing sports bars to celebrate the action. Additional details on participating nations, team rosters, schedules, and tickets are coming soon. record.title: Lez Zeppelin: The Song Remains The Same - 50th Anniversary Celebration
record.address: 220 N. Washington Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
record.description: Lez Zeppelin celebrates 50 years of Led Zeppelin at The State Theatre on Saturday, November 14th, 2026. Doors open at 7:00 p.m. with showtime at 8:30 p.m. Founded in 2004 by New York guitarist Steph Paynes, this all-girl quartet has gained unanimous critical acclaim as one of the most exciting live acts around, becoming the first female rock act to pay homage to Led Zeppelin while garnering rave reviews worldwide. Lez Zeppelin stays true to the musically audacious spirit of the original, delivering Led Zeppelin's blistering arrangements and monstrous sound note-for-note at sold-out shows globally. In June 2013, Jimmy Page attended their London show and said of the group: "they played the led zeppelin music with an extraordinary sensuality and an energy and passion that highlighted their superb musicianship." What sets Lez Zeppelin apart is their seamless, unique injection of gender-bending performance into the original material. Featured on major television including BBC, CNN, ABC, CBS, MTV, VH-1, and Fox, plus radio shows like Sirius XM and NPR, their first studio album was produced by legendary Eddie Kramer (Led Zeppelin, Jimi Hendrix). Their second LP, Lez Zeppelin I, authentically remakes Led Zeppelin's debut using the same vintage equipment from 1968. From 40,000-person performances at Times Square to Bonnaroo, Hellfest, and the Isle of Wight, plus twice at Madison Square Garden, Lez Zeppelin has broken both glass and class ceilings. Tickets are $30 advance or $34 day of show. Attendees must be 18 or older to enter unless accompanied by a parent; valid ID is required. Lez Zeppelin offers far more than a tribute—it's a transformative celebration of classic rock excellence at The State Theatre in the Fairfax County area, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Mental Reset: Sound Bath + Reiki : Thursday Evenings in Falls Church
record.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
record.description: Thursday is a weird day. The week isn't over, but you are. Mental Reset is one hour at the end of the workday where nobody needs anything from you. You come in, you lie down on a mat, you get a blanket and a bolster, and for the next sixty minutes your only job is to listen. I play crystal singing bowls, guide you through a short meditation so your mind has something to do besides replay the day, and offer Reiki while you rest. Most people tell me some version of the same thing afterward: the noise in their head finally turned down. Not off: down. Enough that they can go home and actually be home, instead of answering emails in their head at the dinner table. You don't need experience. You don't need to know how to meditate, and you definitely don't need to “clear your mind.” If you could do that, you wouldn't need this class. First-timers are in the room most weeks. There are ten spots. That's deliberate. It's a small room, I can see everyone in it, and it never feels like an event. It feels like an exhale. A few regulars started as skeptics; more than one of our Google reviews comes from someone who arrived doubting the whole thing and left surprised at how settled they felt. You don't have to believe in anything for an hour of sound and rest to do you some good. Run by Victoria Vita: CPA for 20+ years, healer for 7+. I sat behind a desk with a brain that wouldn't switch off for a long time before I found this work. Thursday nights are built for the person I used to be. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Come straight from work. Leave like the week let go of you first. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket, and bolster everything is here; you bring nothing • Small group: 10 people maximum, same teacher every week • Time at the end to sit up slowly, have water, and not rush out Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Michael McDermott
record.description: Jammin' Java welcomes singer-songwriter Michael McDermott on Thursday, November 20th, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. Chicago native McDermott has occupied a peculiar and essential place in American music for thirty-plus years: extravagantly praised by Stephen King, The Washington Post, and The Hollywood Reporter, yet perpetually on the verge of the recognition his artistry demands. Raised on the dual gospel of early Dylan and the Stones, Tom Waits and the Who, Woody Guthrie and Van Morrison, McDermott has never made a record that fits neatly into a marketing category—a restless refusal to be contained that makes him essential. His forthcoming album Flowers From The Graveyard (arriving August 21, 2027) collects 11 self-penned songs moving fluidly between anthemic rock and bruised introspection, between political fury and hard-won philosophical calm. The Hollywood Reporter notes "Despair never sounded so good," while Stephen King calls him "one of the best songwriters in the world." The Washington Post suggests "McDermott may prove to be one of his generation's greatest talents." This intimate performance delivers the uncompromising songwriting, raw emotional depth, and masterful artistry that define one of America's most important voices. Admission is $34.00 plus fees. Michael McDermott combines lyrical excellence, unflinching humanity, and timeless rock 'n' roll soul in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Nick Moss Band
record.description: Since first forming The Nick Moss Band featuring Dennis Gruenling in 2016, master blues guitarist Nick Moss and world-class harmonica virtuoso Dennis Gruenling have become torchbearers for traditional electric blues. But rather than simply repeating what’s come before, the band’s high-energy take on old school Chicago, Texas and West Coast sounds is completely their own. With their new Alligator Records release (their third for the label), Get Your Back Into It!, Chicago native Moss and New Jersey native Gruenling—together with Rodrigo Mantovani on bass, and Pierce Downer on drums—deliver a deeply rooted, timeless blue collar blues album. AllMusic says the band, winners of the 2020 & 2024 Blues Music Award for Blues Band Of The Year, “makes the case for the vitality of old-fashioned Chicago electric blues in the 21st century.” They are among the world’s very best old school blues ensembles, with each musician expertly playing off the others. “We are a rare breed as far as how authentic we like to keep the music, while also keeping it up-to-date and exciting,” says Moss. Among many awards and recognitions the band has received, Nick Moss garnered the 2019 Blues Music Award for Best Traditional Blues Male Artist. The band took home Blues Music Awards in 2020 for Album of the Year, Song of the Year, and Band of the Year. In 2024 the band received the prestigious Band of the Year honors again from the Blues Music Awards. Bandmates Dennis Gruenling and Rodrigo Mantovani have been nominated multiple times in their respective categories for instrumentalist harmonica and bass. Dennis also received the award for Best Harmonica Instrumentalist in 2019. Nick Moss proudly represents the city of Chicago as one of the few bluesmen working today to have learned his craft firsthand, directly from many of the genre’s original creators…and rest assured that the band will bring you the best in authentic Blues! record.title: Robert Ellis
record.description: Recorded live to tape in just two days, Robert Ellis’s exquisite new album, Yesterday’s News, is as stripped-down as it gets, with the celebrated songwriter and producer’s delicate, reedy tenor accompanied only by nylon string guitar, upright bass, and the occasional piece of handheld percussion. The arrangements are harmonically sophisticated here, drawing on the open tunings and intricate fingerpicking of English songwriters like Nick Drake or Richard Thompson, and Ellis’s performances are similarly subtle and nuanced, tapping into the bittersweet longing of Chet Baker and the playful poignancy of Bill Evans and Jim Hall. While that might seem surprising coming off 2019’s raucous Texas Piano Man, subverting expectations is nothing new for Ellis. Born and raised outside Houston, he gained early acclaim for his piercing introspection and absorbing narratives, but over the course of five solo albums, he flirted with everything from Paul Simon and John Prine to Elton John and Joni Mitchell in a series of sonic and visual transformations that ran the gamut from Redneck Steely Dan to Lone Star Liberace. NPR hailed his “musical daring and impeccable songcraft,” while Rolling Stone praised his “sharp eye for storytelling,” and the New York Times lauded his writing as an emotional “gut punch.” Yesterday’s News marks Ellis’s debut LP for Niles City Records, an outgrowth of the famed Niles City Sound studio he and longtime collaborator Josh Block run in Fort Worth, TX. record.description: Roger Waters will not be at this performance. The father’s legacy. The son’s band. Roger Waters Presents LEGACY - A Pink Floyd Show is an all-new live production celebrating the defining music and visual world of Pink Floyd’s golden era from 1971-1979. Created under the direction of Roger Waters with a band led by his son Harry Waters, a longtime touring musician, pianist and composer, LEGACY features a world-class 10-piece band performing the ground breaking songs from The Dark Side of the Moon, Wish You Were Here, Animals and The Wall. Harry, who spent more than 15 years performing alongside his father, serves as musical director and leads the band on B3 organ, piano and vocals. Musically, the production aims to recreate the original recordings as closely as possible, while the stage presentation shaped by Roger’s team features a pictorial retrospective of imagery inspired by the original Pink Floyd work, including visuals Roger created during his tenure as the band’s creative force, all presented on high-definition LED video screens. Spanning more than two hours, LEGACY reaches deep into Pink Floyd’s catalog and celebrates the music that defined a generation, music that is just as relevant today. record.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
record.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
record.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

record.title: The American Story
record.description: The National Archives Museum debuts a once-in-a generation redesign of its permanent exhibits: The American Story and the Discovery Center - connecting visitors with the National Archives in revolutionary ways. The American Story will showcase items and records in the National Archives that tell important moments in our nation's history. Visitors will get up close to more than 40 original artifacts and documents, including a rare 1823 Stone Engraving of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's annotated copy of the Constitution, and presidential gifts including horseshoes to President Bush from Queen Elizabeth II. The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

record.description: On Sunday, November 15, at 4:00 PM, the St. Andrew the Apostle Concert Series proudly welcomes The Catholic University of America Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Maestro Simeone Tartaglione, for a free afternoon of orchestral masterworks. Program Paul Dukas – The Sorcerer’s Apprentice Camille Saint-Saëns – Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor Vasily Popov, cello Camille Saint-Saëns – Symphony No. 3 in C minor, “Organ Symphony” Michael Murphy, organ The centerpiece is Saint-Saëns’ thrilling Organ Symphony, which integrates the pipe organ into two of its four movements for a powerful blend of orchestral color and majestic organ sound. Performing on the St. Andrew Pipe Organ of the Holy Archangels—a French Romantic instrument installed by the Peragallo Pipe Organ Company in 2020 (three manuals, 51 ranks, 2,891 pipes)—organist Michael Murphy will bring the work’s full intended glory to life. The program opens with Dukas’ vivid symphonic poem, famously featured in Disney’s Fantasia, followed by one of the most beloved cello concertos of the 19th century. This concert is ideal for anyone who appreciates masterful composition, virtuoso performance, and the transcendent beauty of live symphonic music in a sacred setting. About the Conductor Maestro Simeone Tartaglione is Associate Professor of Practice in Instrumental Music at The Catholic University of America’s Rome School of Performing Arts, where he serves as Conducting Area Head and conductor of the university orchestra. Trained in the European tradition at Rome’s Santa Cecilia Conservatory and with advanced degrees including a Doctorate in Philology, he has conducted across Europe, the United States, South Africa, and beyond. He currently serves as Music Director of the Newark Symphony Orchestra and Delaware Youth Symphony, among others. He is the recipient of the prestigious 2025 Telamone Prize. record.title: The Civil War
record.description: From 1861 to 1865, Americans fought each other with a ferocity unseen in the country’s history. The immediate cause of the war was the secession of the Southern states. However, the roots lay in growing tensions over slavery. By the time the last shots were fired, as many as 750,000 Americans had been killed, and four million enslaved people were freed. This traveling banner exhibition, from the Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History, examines the impact of the Civil War on Americans throughout the fractured nation. With meticulous attention to detail — from lush chorus-drenched guitars and melodic bass lines to dynamic stage presence — the band transports audiences back to the golden age of postpunk and gothic alternative. Whether performing beloved tracks like “Just Like Heaven,” “A Forest,” and “Lovesong,” or diving deep into fan-favorite cuts, The Gathering Gloom celebrates the music that defined moods, movements, and memories. record.title: The Kennedys CD Release & Maura’s Birthday Party
record.description: The Kennedys, a duo strong for more than 30 years, have recorded two dozen collections of mostly original songs while establishing themselves as core artists on the AAA and Americana charts. Touring at 50,000 miles per year before the pandemic, they also hosted "The Dharma Café" on Sirius/XM radio for four years. When Covid struck, they pivoted seamlessly, performing over 150 livestreams and playing 1,000+ songs for a global audience. Now back on the road and active in the studio, Pete and Maura are preparing Smoketree, their 2026 release and follow-up to 2023's Headwinds, which spent a month at #1 on the national Folk DJ chart. Smoketree consists of newly written original songs reflecting their feelings on environmental concerns, social upheaval, and the search for peace—both global and personal. True to their trademark approach, they bring uplift and encouragement rather than simply cursing the darkness. Well-traveled and never tiring of the wandering troubadour life, The Kennedys continue their blend of energized folk-rock, passion, and genuine camaraderie with their audience. Jammin' Java welcomes this enduring force to Fairfax County, Virginia.

record.title: The Last Bison
record.description: Jammin' Java welcomes The Last Bison on Wednesday, December 10th, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. In 2012, The Last Bison rose from the marshes of southeastern Virginia to captivate the national music scene with a rare blend of music that NPR dubbed "Classical influenced southern folk rock." The band has drawn comparisons to indie superstars including Mumford & Sons, The Decemberists, and Fleet Foxes, harvesting a dynamic, anthemic sound from the soil of their folk roots. The Last Bison's self-released debut album Quill captured textured, poetic waves "threaded with their own singular strands of creativity," according to NoiseTrade, while WXPN of Philadelphia noted the band "has subsequently swept the musical scene with its complex arrangements, refined lyrics and vocal harmonies." Following Quill (2011) and their Universal Republic Records release Inheritance (2013), The Last Bison self-produced the 2014 album VA in an old A-frame cabin called "the Wigwam" on the edge of the Great Dismal Swamp near Chesapeake, Virginia. The album's organic drums and booming energy showcase the band's sonic evolution. The most recent work SÜDA, tracked at COLLECTOR Studios in Norfolk in summer 2016, moves the music into technicolor with expanded arrangements inspired by frontman Ben Hardesty's childhood in the Bolivian rainforests. SÜDA explores themes of longing, remembered times, and spiritual catharsis while maintaining the intimate chamber folk sensibility that originally drew fans to the music. The ensemble features Ben Hardesty (primary songwriter/vocals), Andrew Benfante (piano/reed organ), Amos Housworth (cello/bass), Dan Hardesty (banjo/mandolin/guitar), Annah Housworth (bells/vocals), and Teresa Totheroh (violin). The Last Bison delivers chamber folk excellence, complex arrangements, and heartfelt artistry in Fairfax County, Virginia. Tickets are $27.00 plus fees. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: The Nth Power
record.description: The Nth Power, featuring guitarist Nick Cassarino, bassist Nate Edgar, and drummer Nikki Glaspie, believes in the healing power of music. The seasoned trio delivers a transcendent blend of soul, funk, rock, and rhythm and blues anchored by multi-part vocal harmonies and elevated musicianship that inspires audiences to dance, groove, or stand transfixed. Aligning in New Orleans during Jazz Fest, The Nth Power's electric live performances have floored audiences ever since. Following their breakout 2013 EP Basic Minimum Skills Test, the band released two acclaimed studio albums and two live albums, earning national coverage in Relix, Modern Drummer, Glide, Paste, and Sirius XM Radio. Their individual credentials include collaborations with Beyoncé, Snarky Puppy, Maceo Parker, Dumpstaphunk, and John Brown's Body. "It's my dream team," said bandleader Glaspie. The Speaks, active from 1997 to 2009, broke down barriers with anthemic music and legendary live shows, earning radio play on DC101 and selling out five consecutive 9:30 Club shows. record.title: The Suitcase Junket
record.description: The Suitcase Junket -- the intriguing songwriter/multi-instrumentalist Matt Lorenz -- weds the sensibilities of early blues and rock ‘n’ roll, the improvisational spirit of jazz, and his love of Tom Waits to meticulous, cultured songcraft. Dubbed a “master of musical imagination” by NPR’s World Café Live and “astonishing” by WBUR Boston, Lorenz’s weathered, howl-flecked voice was described by Rochester City Newspaper as “a cross between Hound Dog Taylor and a Tuvan throat singer who has swallowed a bird.” Lorenz has earned snowballing acclaim for his achingly poetic dark folk. A solitary artist with an organic yet ornate vision, his seventh album To Go On is his most acutely profound yet. Created in the wake of losing his sister, singer-songwriter Kate Lorenz, it’s a tender, beautiful, and arrestingly moving record; an internal dialogue and conversation with the departed, enormously resonant to anyone who ever loved anyone. record.title: TRSH – Gone Fishin' Tour
record.description: TRSH exists in the tension between extremes, a tightrope walk that’s volatile and unpredictable yet built on intentional detail. The Springfield, MO quartet has blurred those lines since forming in 2021, childhood friends frustrated by false starts and determined to start a new project in what frontman Derek Berry calls a “last-ditch effort” to make their musical dreams a reality. “I was like 23 with a newborn baby and felt like, ‘If it doesn't work, it doesn't work, and if it does, that's cool,’” Berry remembers. It quickly did, with the group’s 2022 debut LP, Kiss Me, breaking through with a fusion of punk and Midwest emo, diary entries set to dexterous guitar work. A prolific series of follow-ups, from singles like “Dad Rock” and their second album, Soporific, to 2024’s Straw Chairs EP, have taken them even further, going viral on social media, racking up more than 15 million collective streams and cementing Berry, Keiran Andrews (bass), Bowen Pennell (drums) and Gunnar Pennell (guitar) as one of the brightest young acts in emo. Now, on their new LP, STRING THEORY (Wax Bodega), TRSH unleash their most explosive collection yet, equal parts introspective and irreverent topped off with powder-keg energy and self-deprecating charm. There are no saints in TRSH’s songs, but no villains either. Instead, tracks like the fervent first single “dusty,” galloping “drown me in a bathtub” and pained “hyperpop killed my dog,” with its gut-punch refrain “I’m falling apart,” are transparently honest portraits of fucking up and falling short: bad decisions that felt right at the time, awkward apologies and late-night spirals. The moments when you should shut up but the voice in your head – aided by anxiety, neurosis or illicit substances – won’t let you stop talking. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: We Make History
record.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

record.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
record.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
record.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

record.title: Hermit Day
record.description: Hermit Day October 29 @ 9:30 am - 4:00 pm Day of Quiet at Bon Secours Do you… need a day of quiet and solitude to rest, reflect, be? need at least one of these each year? sense that God may be inviting you to enter silence and reorient? October 29 th might be just for you, as it is the annual celebration of National Hermit Day. Although its origins are not firmly known, many attribute Hermit Day’s origin to the 18th century and suggest a connection to the Irish Hermit Saint Colman. It gives us an opportunity to join the many others who — throughout Christian history — have entered silence and solitude to remember what is most important: to listen, to pray. A day like this has the potential to initiate or strengthen a regular practice. Since 2014, Bon Secours Retreat and Conference Center has hosted Quiet Morning events that are also opportunities for shared silence. This day will follow a similar pattern. We will begin and end together in simple prayer, have lunch in shared silence, and spend the day on our own in prayer or other quiet activities such as walking, doing art, reading, journaling — whatever you feel inclined to do. The Center’s daily Mass at 11:00 am will be available to you, if desired. This is mostly a silent retreat. Lunch is included. Guided by Joanne Cahoon.

record.title: Alison Brown Quintet
record.description: A Bold New Sound in American Banjo Music One of the most innovative minds in roots music, Alison Brown is a Grammy-winning musician and Grammy-nominated producer known for taking the banjo far beyond its Appalachian roots. Blending bluegrass and jazz influences, Brown creates a rich sonic tapestry that has earned praise from The Wall Street Journal , CBS Sunday Morning , NPR, and USA Today . In 2025, Brown teamed up with actor and musician Steve Martin to release the collaborative album Safe, Sensible and Sane . The longtime friends and banjo devotees crafted a collection of banjo-inspired songs pairing Brown’s daringly inventive melodies and Martin’s idiosyncratic yet ineffably tender lyrics. Featuring guest appearances by Jackson Browne, Vince Gill, Indigo Girls, Tim O’Brien, Jason Mraz, and Della Mae, the album marks a captivating new chapter in the evolution of banjo music. Learn more about this performance and Alison Brown on her official website . This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s LIVE! Series , celebrating iconic music and exceptional musicianship. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and excellent acoustics for a memorable concert experience.

record.title: Asleep at the Wheel
record.description: Asleep at the Wheel has been a defining force in Texas and Western Swing music for over five decades. Since 1970, the band has featured more than 100 members, with lineup changes often inspiring new recordings and continued evolution. Although the band got its start on a farm in Paw Paw, West Virginia, they became a cornerstone of the Austin, Texas scene upon its arrival in 1973. Inspired by Western swing and honky-tonk country, the band has accrued 10 Grammy Awards. A key element of the band’s sound remains the fiddle, now featuring vocalist and fiddler Ian Stewart, whose connection to Austin’s music scene helped lead him to the group. Band leader Ray Benson and Stewart both emphasize Asleep at the Wheel’s deep Texas roots, musical mentorship, and ongoing commitment to honoring and evolving Western Swing traditions through energetic live performance and collaboration. Learn more about Asleep at the Wheel by visiting their official website. This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s LIVE! Series , celebrating iconic music and exceptional musicianship. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and excellent acoustics for a memorable concert experience.

Don’t miss another glorious concert featuring Calvary UMC’s Cornel Zimmer 46-rank, 4-manual pipe organ. Mr. Aune, who holds a doctorate of musical arts from Eastman School of Music, teaches at Peabody Institute and is the director of music and organist at Christ Lutheran Church in Baltimore. His program will include organ works by well-known composers, highlighting the many colors and sounds of Calvary UMC’s organ. This concert is sponsored in part by The Frederick Arts Council, The Delaplaine Foundation, and the William E. Cross Foundation. https://peabody.jhu.edu/faculty/Daniel-Aune/

record.title: Calvary UMC's Community Concert Series presents District5 Quintet
record.description: Calvary United Methodist Church (calvaryumc.org/concerts) located in historic downtown Frederick presents District5 Quintet, a woodwind group. Their program, “Better Together: Music for Resilience,” invites you to rediscover what brings us together in a divided world. This isn’t just a concert—it’s an experience of community—where you can pause, breathe, and reconnect through music. Through a series of stunningly beautiful and powerful works, including music by Bernstein, Copland, and Grieg, they’ll explore how music offers unity and resilience. This concert is sponsored in part by The Frederick Arts Council, The Delaplaine Foundation, and the William E. Cross Foundation. www.District5Quintet.org

record.title: Calvary UMC's Community Concert Series presents Duo Fuerza, four-hand piano
record.description: Calvary United Methodist Church(calvaryumc.org/concerts) located in historic downtown Frederick presents international Steinway Artist James D’León and acclaimed pianist Alwen Yeung. Join us as they ignite the stage with electrifying four-hand piano performances that blend virtuosity, precision, and visual artistry with dynamic energy to a diverse program: the refined elegance of Johann Sebastian Bach, the lyricism of Franz Schubert, the rhythmic fire of Astor Piazzolla, the jazz brilliance of George Gershwin, and the dazzling virtuosity of Nikolai Kapustin. Duo Fuerza delivers a concert experience that captivates audiences of all backgrounds. This concert is sponsored in part by The Frederick Arts Council, The Delaplaine Foundation, and the William E. Cross Foundation. www.DuoFeurza.com

record.title: Celebrating 40 Years of Wine Making in Frederick County
record.description: Frederick County is home to three of Maryland's oldest wineries, each with a legacy dating back to the 1970s and 1980s. record.title: CENTENNIAL Event: John Pizzarelli presents DEAR MR. BENNETT
record.description: John Pizzarelli presents: Dear Mr. Bennett – A Tribute to Tony Bennett . Grammy Award-winning producer and guitarist extraordinaire, John Pizzarelli salutes the legendary Tony Bennett, celebrating over 60 years of unparalleled artistry. From Bennett’s ’50s pop hits like “Because of You” and “Rags to Riches” through his timeless classics of the ’60s such as “I Wanna Be Around” and “I Left My Heart in San Francisco,” to his remarkable collaborations with Bill Evans, Pizzarelli’s trio will bring these iconic songs to life once again. The show will also highlight Bennett’s incredible revival in the ‘90s while Pizzarelli weaves in personal anecdotes and stories that reveal the man behind the music. The John Pizzarelli Trio honors this generational talent in a night of stellar musicianship. Learn more about this show and John Pizzarelli on his official website. record.title: CENTENNIAL Event: Lee Rocker of The Stray Cats
record.description: Lee Rocker made his mark singing, playing, standing on, spinning, and rocking his giant upright bass as a founding member of the Grammy-nominated music group the STRAY CATS . The Stray Cats sold over 10 million albums, garnered 23 gold and platinum certified records, and were among the early music-video pioneers of MTV. The Stray Cats’ worldwide mega hits, “Rock This Town,” “Stray Cat Strut,” and “Sexy and Seventeen” have become a part of the fabric of rock n roll. From appearing on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine and as the musical guest on Saturday Night Live , to headlining the world’s biggest festivals and touring with the Rolling Stones, Lee Rocker has seen and done it all! In addition to his career with the Stray Cats, Lee Rocker has recorded and performed with George Harrison, Ringo Starr, Willie Nelson, Leon Russell, John Fogerty, and Carl Perkins. Rocker has also received numerous honors for his contributions to music and the arts, including being inducted to the Bass Player Hall of Fame, the Rockabilly Hall of Fame, the Long Island Music Hall of Fame, and he is a recipient of the Visionary Artist Award by his home city of Laguna Beach, California. To learn more about Lee Rocker, visit his official website . This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s Centennial Events, celebrating 100 years of entertainment in our historic building. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and timeless atmosphere for a meaningful entertainment experience.

record.title: CENTENNIAL FILM Series: Cabin in the Sky (1943)
record.description: A Musical Battle Between Good & Evil Cabin in the Sky follows Little Joe, a man who, after being killed over gambling debts, awakens in purgatory and is granted six months back on Earth to redeem himself and prove he deserves entry into Heaven. His journey through faith, love, and moral conflict unfolds through a series of musical performances that reflect both earthly temptation and heavenly intervention. Featuring music by Duke Ellington and his Orchestra , Cabin in the Sky blends gospel, jazz, and theatrical storytelling into a rich stylized musical fantasy. The film is notable for its all-Black cast, making it an important early example of mainstream Hollywood representation during the Golden Age of cinema. Combining vivid fantasy sequences, moral allegory, and elaborate musical staging, Cabin in the Sky remains a visually striking and culturally significant work celebrated for its artistry, performances, and lasting historical importance. record.title: CENTENNIAL FILM Series: Singin’ in the Rain (1952)
record.description: One of the Most Beloved Musical Films of All Time Singin’ in the Rain represents Hollywood’s transition from silent cinema to “talkies.” Set during the late 1920s, the story follows silent film star Don Lockwood, played by Gene Kelly , as he navigates the challenges of sound technology entering the film industry. When his leading lady’s voice proves unsuitable for talking pictures, a young aspiring actress, played by Debbie Reynolds , steps in to save the production. Featuring iconic performances by Gene Kelly, Debbie Reynolds, and Donald O’Connor, the film is renowned for its musical numbers, including the legendary title sequence. This musical blends romance, comedy, and satire with dazzling choreography and timeless songs, making it a landmark of American cinema.
