record.title: CENTENNIAL FILM Series: Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? (1962)
record.description: Psychological Horror that Still Shocks What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? is a psychological thriller that remains one of Hollywood’s most acclaimed Gothic dramas. Starring Bette Davis as Jane Hudson, a former child performer whose career has faded, and Joan Crawford as her sister Blanche, a once-successful actress now confined to a wheelchair. As old rivalries and long-buried resentments resurface, the sisters’ secluded mansion becomes the setting for a chilling struggle marked by manipulation, obsession, and revenge. Renowned for its powerful performances, tense atmosphere, and shocking narrative twists, What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? became a critical and commercial success upon its release. The film helped shape the psychological horror genre and remains a landmark of American cinema, captivating audiences with its exploration of fame, jealousy, and family conflict. record.title: DISCOVERY Series: Crys Matthews
record.description: A New Southern Voice & the Sound of Social Justice “A troubadour of truth,” Nashville resident Crys Matthews is among the brightest stars of the new generation of social justice music makers. An award-winning lyricist and composer, Matthews blends country, Americana, folk, blues, and bluegrass into bold, complex performances steeped in traditional melodies and honest, original lyrics. Her mission? To amplify the voices of the unheard, shed light on the unseen, and be a steadfast reminder that hope and love are the truest pathways to equity and justice. Her new album, Reclamation , reflects that mission. Recorded in Nashville, Tennessee, at Sound Emporium Studios, Reclamation was produced by Levi Lowry and features collaborators including Heather Mae, Kyshona, Melody Walker, and Chris Housman, along with top Music City musicians. Matthews, a preacher’s child, Black woman, lesbian, and proud Southerner, uses her music to reclaim space in country and Americana music, expand representation for LGBTQ+ communities in faith spaces, and honor the South that raised her. Learn more about this show and Crys Matthews by visiting her official website . This show is part of the Discovery Series , presented by The Tivoli Society. New Spire Stages , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers an intimate venue for a memorable concert experience.

record.title: DISCOVERY Series: Lost Mary
record.description: The Soundtrack of Front Porches, Late Nights & Smoky Basements Lost Mary is the songwriting project of Luke Martin and David Johnson III. Hailing from the small, rural town of Hillsdale, Michigan, this duo is committed to the essence of folk music storytelling. Pulling from both traditional and modern folk and Americana influences, they bring together their unique musical backgrounds to create songs and stories that are as personal as they are universal. Their work reflects a deep respect for narrative-driven songwriting, with arrangements that emphasize acoustic textures and lyrical clarity. By blending lived experience with regional imagery, Lost Mary crafts songs that resonate with themes of home, memory, and human connection, continuing the folk tradition while shaping a contemporary voice rooted in authenticity. This show is part of the Discovery Series , presented by The Tivoli Society. New Spire Stages , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers an intimate venue for a memorable concert experience.

record.title: DISCOVERY Series: Rabbitology
record.description: Evocative Sonic Storytelling Everyone has their own world: fragments of moments lived, translated, and understood through metaphor and storytelling. Rabbitology is the music project of Nat Timmerman, a world pulled from her odd-running mind. Venture into these eclectic soundscapes and discover a collection of memoirs turned into fantastical sonic short stories. Strange but charming, you will find these songs bundled in capes of star-dusted moss, grounded in the natural world, and propelled by the raw and the real. If a song takes place in the woods, then the woods the song will become; the percussion is the stomping of the leaves, the synth is a warped fox’s cry. Thus arise the stories of dread-gray skies, writhing vines, and shivering pines, stories of a magically real folk horror. The dark and ugly become beautiful here, and vice versa. In this world, there is no such thing as “black or white,” instead, everything exists together at once. To learn more about Rabbitology and Nat Timmerman, visit her official website . record.title: Exhibition Openings: FOCUS at The Delaplaine
record.description: Exhibition Openings: FOCUS at The Delaplaine Saturday, November 7 • 3–5 pm FREE View exhibitions and meet the artists! These exhibitions are opening on Saturday, November 7 and can be viewed starting at 9 am. Beat the crowds and visit us earlier in the day! Nov 7–29 National Juried Photography Exhibition Part of FOCUS: A Celebration of Photography, the NJPE takes place every other year in November. The exhibition features selected photographs by regional and national artists. ABOUT THE JUROR: E. Brady Robinson is a Baltimore-based photographer and creative director known for her vibrant and eclectic mix of fine art photography, cultural documentation, and portraits of creatives. Her work has been featured in solo and group exhibitions in the US and internationally, and her photographs are held in the permanent collections of the Orlando Museum of Art and the Spanish Cultural Center in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Robinson teaches photography and senior seminar at Georgetown University and is a contributing photographer for BmoreArt and Baltimore Beat. Nov 7–29 Mark Seaver Beauty Through Thin Ice Photography Seaver’s photography uses ice and its properties as a filter through which to photograph. The result is the refraction of light, which distorts and abstracts the world seen through it. Nov 7–29 Christophe Casamassima The Dirty Window Photography The Dirty Window is a phantasmagoric cycle of photography that aligns with the four stages of sleep. Casamassima uses photography to explore how repetition reveals difference and where latent images surface to consciousness before dissolving again. Nov 7–29 Kevin Stivers Elsewhere Photography Elsewhere exists between places, neither here nor there. The work in Stiver’s exhibition explores themes of human connection and disconnect and feelings of belonging and misplacement, shrouded in a surreal atmosphere.

record.title: FACETED Seminar Series | Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving
record.description: Join the InBloom team on Saturday, November 7th at 3PM in their Downtown Frederick gallery for the next talk in the FACETED seminar series— Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving . A hand-engraved line isn’t simply applied to jewelry—it deliberately transforms the metal. For centuries, engravers have cut controlled lines into metal to preserve names, create intricate patterns, and bring surfaces and stories to life through texture, light, and shadow. It’s a beautiful expression of InBloom Jewelry’ philosophy: artistry in service to love. Whether a meaningful date inside a band, a name rendered in script, or a hand-cut design inspired by a personal story, hand engraving makes jewelry deeply personal and enduring—meticulously carved by a person, for a person (or by the InBloom goldsmiths, for you). This seminar will include a fascinating discussion on the history and evolution of hand engraving and a live demonstration of this centuries-old art form. Free to all, RSVPs encouraged.

record.title: Frederick in the Civil War
record.venue: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
record.description: History, Heroics, and the Occasional Amputation (Strictly Metaphorical) Right, gather round, you historically curious lot! Step smartly aboard as we begin our highly educational meander from the National Museum of Civil War Medicine in Downtown Frederick, Maryland, where you’ll learn how doctors once treated nearly everything with brandy, saws, and an unwavering sense of optimism. Your guide, a certified docent and part-time time traveler, will regale you with tales of battlefield brilliance, questionable hygiene, and the astonishing resilience of people who really ought to have taken the day off. So join us for a Frederick Civil War history tour because this isn’t just history… it’s history on the double, with a head wound and a bandage made from curtains. Perfect for history buffs, museum lovers, and anyone searching for unique things to do in Frederick, Maryland, this unforgettable Civil War bus tour offers a delightfully British take on America’s most dramatic century.

record.title: Frederick Speaker Series: Adam Richman
record.description: Food Enthusiast & TV Personality Born and raised in Brooklyn, Adam Richman’s passion for diverse culinary specialties and all things edible was ignited by his early experiences in the food mecca of NYC. Long before discovering his thirst for travel, Adam had access to authentic delicacies from around the globe, all within the borders of his diverse Brooklyn neighborhood. However, it was cooking a plain cheese omelet with his Aunt Anne that became a defining moment of his early years; watching simple ingredients transform from basic staples into a versatile composed dish was revelatory for a young Adam, igniting his fascination with the culinary world. Widely known as the host of one of the Travel Channel’s highest rated shows, Man v. Food , Adam also hosted the network’s Secret Eats with Adam Richman . He hosted and co-executive produced Man v. Food Nation , Adam Richman’s Best Sandwich in America , Fandemonium , and hosted NBC’s food competition show Food Fighters . Adam’s first book, America the Edible (Rodale Publishing, 2010), offers a behind-the-scenes look at his adventures traveling—and eating, of course—across the U.S. In 2015, inspired by the many great cuisines sampled during his travels, Adam penned his first cookbook, Straight Up Tasty (Clarkson Potter), featuring his signature take on globally inspired comfort food. This show is part of The Frederick Speaker Series . Now in its 14th season, The Frederick Speaker Series has developed a reputation for bringing world-class speakers to the Frederick area. The Series aims to engage the community through enlightening discourse and meaningful topics. As a result, Frederick’s reputation as an intellectual hub continues to grow, drawing audiences from D.C., Baltimore, and beyond.

record.title: Frederick Speaker Series: MIA HAMM
record.description: World Cup & Olympic Champion After 17 years, two World Championships, two Olympic Gold Medals, and near unparalleled success as a marketing icon, Mia Hamm retired from professional soccer in 2004. Not only as the best women’s soccer player in history, but also as one of the most important and recognizable female figures in the history of sport. Hailed by ESPN as the greatest female athlete of the past 40 years, Mia was the youngest woman to ever appear in a match for the US Senior Squad at just 15 years old in 1987. Her illustrious career that followed playing for the national team shattered a litany of American records, most notably those for international goals (158) and assists (144). In the years since her dominant run on the global stage as a player, Mia has continued to serve as an inspiration to young girls looking to rise to the pinnacle of the sporting world. Indeed, she has maintained an active presence within the soccer community and has served as an outspoken advocate for Title IX and gender equality across sporting lines—all the while cementing her status as the face of not merely a sport but rather of an entire generation of female athletes through her Foundation. record.description: NYT Bestselling Author of The Correspondent Virginia Evans is the author of the #1 New York Times bestselling novel The Correspondent , which constructs a narrative through letters and emails—some sent, others unsent—to and from Sybil Van Antwerp as she ages and loses her sight, creating a shifting view of her past and future. The Correspondent won the 2026 PEN/Hemingway Award for Debut Novel, inaugural James Patterson & Bookshop.org Prize (celebrating debut authors), and the Indies Choice Book Award for Adult Fiction. It was a Best Book of the Year for NPR, the Washington Post , Boston Globe , Elle , Christian Science Monitor , Amazon, She Reads , and was a BBC Radio 2 Book Club pick. record.title: GET THE LED OUT
record.description: A Soul-stirring Tribute to Led Zeppelin From the bombastic and epic, to the folky and mystical, Get The Led Out (GTLO) have captured the essence of the recorded music of Led Zeppelin and brought it to the concert stage. The Philadelphia-based group consists of six veteran musicians intent on delivering Led Zeppelin live, like you’ve never heard before. Utilizing the multi-instrumentalists at their disposal, GTLO recreate the songs in all their depth and glory with the studio overdubs that Zeppelin themselves never performed. When you hear three guitars on the album…GTLO delivers three guitars on stage. No wigs or fake English accents, GTLO brings what the audience wants…a high-energy Zeppelin concert with an honest, heart-thumping intensity. Dubbed by the media as “The American Led Zeppelin”, Get the Led Out offer strong focus on the early years of Zeppelin. They also touch on the deeper cuts that were sledom, if ever, heard in concert. GTLO also include a special “acoustic set” with Zep favorites such as “Tangerine” and “Hey Hey What Can I Do.” A GTLO concert mimics the “light and shade” that are the embodiment of “the Mighty Zep.” Whether it’s the passion and fury with which they deliver the blues-soaked, groove-driven rock anthems, it’s their attention to detail and nuance that makes a Get The Led Out performance a truly awe-inspiring event! Learn more about this event at the official Get the Led Out website . Tickets go on sale to Members at 10 am on September 17 and to the Public at 10 am on September 22. This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s LIVE! Series , celebrating iconic music and exceptional musicianship. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and excellent acoustics for a memorable concert experience.

record.description: Our time spent together will invite spaciousness and curiosity. We will tune into our senses, learn and practice somatic safety exercises, and deepen relationship with Earth community. The breadth of invitations will include body-based somatic safety practices that you can do anywhere, landscape-based somatic safety practices that tend the nervous system in relationship with Earth, mindfulness practices, and meditations. record.title: Haunted History at The National Museum of Civil War Medicine
record.venue: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
record.description: Starting on October 10th, tour the most haunted building in Frederick – the National Museum of Civil War Medicine. Explore the building’s history amidst the darkened galleries and offices. On the tour, staff and volunteers will share stories of Civil War embalmers, the building’s most infamous tenants, and their first-hand accounts of paranormal activity that have given the building its spooky reputation. In addition to a trip through the museum galleries, the tour provides exclusive access to the third floor where numerous sightings have occurred. 48 East Patrick Street was built in the 1830s. Before it became the National Museum of Civil War Medicine, the building was a furniture shop and a site of Civil War embalming, as well as home to many Frederick residents and their businesses. The past still echoes through the halls of the building. The haunting sights, sounds, and sensations from the building have been reported for decades by the people who lived and worked in the building over many years. Join us to hear our staff and volunteers’ stories first-hand. You are invited to bring your own cameras and ghost-finding apps – who knows what you’ll capture! Flash photography and LIVE streaming are prohibited. Tours will be given on October 10, 17, 24, and 25, from 5:30 p.m.-6:30 p.m. This year we are offering two special Halloween tours on Saturday, October 31, from 5:30 p.m.-8:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m.-10:30 p.m. During these special Halloween night tours, you’ll have additional time to tour the galleries without a guide.
record.categories: Civil War, History & Heritage, Holiday Events, Tours, Downtown Frederick
record.admission: $30 for the general public; $20 for museum members

record.title: History on the Double
record.description: Two decks, one timeline, and absolutely no sense of direction. Good morning, historians, adventurers, and anyone who got on the wrong bus but is too polite to admit it! Perfect for families, visitors, history lovers, and anyone looking for fun things to do in Frederick Maryland, this unforgettable historical sightseeing tour is your front-row seat to the city’s remarkable past, served with a generous helping of British wit.

record.title: Legends & Lore
record.description: Come see the darker side of Frederick. When night falls, Frederick’s familiar streets have rather different stories to tell. Climb aboard our vintage double-decker for an hour of dark tales from Frederick’s past , researched from local histories, old accounts and the legends that have lingered long after the people involved have gone. As we make our way through the city, we’ll slow down at the very places connected to these stories, from historic streets and old buildings to some of Frederick’s more famously haunted places . Along the way, you’ll hear tales of strange happenings, restless spirits and the darker chapters of local history, all told against the backdrop of Frederick after dark. And because it’s October, you’ll also get a rather good view from the top deck as the city’s historic homes and neighborhoods put on their best autumn and Halloween displays. Whether you’re a believer, a skeptic, or simply enjoy a good story with a slightly unsettling ending, Legends and Lore offers a different way to discover Frederick’s history. Just remember, it’s much easier to laugh at a ghost story when you’re not sitting on the top deck in the dark. TOUR HIGHLIGHTS Hear researched tales of Frederick’s haunted places, local legends and darker history, told where the stories happened. Experience Frederick after dark from the top deck, with historic streets, autumn displays and a few places you’ll look at rather differently afterwards. record.title: Luca Stricagnoli
record.description: Redefining the Acoustic Guitar With his music videos receiving more than 200 million internet views and bookings in every corner of the globe, Luca Stricagnoli is considered one of the most unique guitarists in the world. Hailed as a phenomenon and a prodigy by influential magazines and newspapers globally, he has performed in over 30 countries and has even been shared by famous bands such as Red Hot Chili Peppers, Metallica, Muse, and Walk Off the Earth. Stricagnoli continues developing performances and instruments that incorporate many unorthodox ideas, including the Reversed Triple Neck Guitar . This instrument—the first reversed neck in guitar history—has greatly contributed to the modern evolution of the acoustic guitar. His viral inventions have skyrocketed his career, with performances at events for Nobel Prize winners and top CEOs, as well as having his music featured in countless television shows. Learn more about this show and Luca Stricagnoli by visiting his official website . This show is part of New Spire Arts’ programming . record.title: Monocacy Battlefield Tour
record.description: The Battle that Saved Washington Battlefields have a remarkable habit of looking peaceful. You’d never guess they were once full of people making spectacularly bad days for one another. On July 9, 1864, Monocacy National Battlefield became the setting for the battle remembered as the “Battle That Saved Washington.” By delaying the Confederate advance on the nation’s capital, the Union forces bought precious time for Washington’s defenses, making Monocacy one of the Civil War’s most significant, and perhaps most underestimated, battlefields. Beginning at the Monocacy Battlefield Visitor Center , we’ll journey through the battlefield with a National Park Service guide who brings the battlefield to life., following the course of the fighting while uncovering the stories of the soldiers who fought here and the families whose homes suddenly found themselves in the middle of history. With an expert guide bringing the landscape to life, you’ll discover how a quiet stretch of Maryland came to play an extraordinary role in the nation’s story. History happened here in a single day. The consequences took rather longer. DURATION: 1 hour DEPARTS FROM: Monocacy National Battlefield, 5201 Urbana Pike Frederick, MD 21704 TICKETING DETAILS: $35 per person. A minimum total of 15 tickets must be sold for the tour to run. If we don’t sell the required minimum of tickets, we’ll gladly refund your purchase or credit it toward another exciting tour. We’re committed to ensuring you have a fantastic experience, and we appreciate your understanding as we work to create fun, unforgettable events together!

record.description: A Civilized Literary Excursion (with Cake) Are you ready to explore Downtown Frederick, Maryland in impeccable style and mild confusion? Your Clippie will escort you on a scenic two-hour Frederick sightseeing tour, pointing out local landmarks, fascinating facts, and the occasional squirrel with suspicious intent. You’ll laugh, you’ll learn, endure discounts and you’ll probably wonder how we got permission for this. First stop: The Curious Iguana , Downtown Frederick’s beloved independent bookstore, home to bestsellers, local authors, and at least one employee who definitely reads too much. Browse to your heart’s content, discover hidden literary gems, or simply pretend you’ve wandered into a BBC period drama about literacy. Then it’s onward to Twin Bears Bakery , where the air smells of happiness, butter, and light moral compromise. There you’ll enjoy handcrafted pastries so good you may consider writing poetry about them (haikus are acceptable). This stop is a highlight among Frederick’s bakery tours, and you’ll quickly understand why it’s a local favourite. Whether you’re a bibliophile, a foodie, or simply looking for unique things to do in Frederick, Maryland, Pages & Pastries is the perfect combination of books, bakeries, and double-decker bus charm. It’s a Frederick city tour for the curious, the hungry, and the happily confused, mixing stories, sweets, and scenic streets into one gloriously crumb-covered adventure. Come hungry. record.title: Re-Leaf Agency
record.description: A Multisensory Performance Prompting Reflection and Action Re-Leaf Agency invites you into an immersive environment of lush movement, rich sounds, provocative text, and larger-than-life video projections of trees, mushrooms, ferns, wildflowers, and streams spanning multiple surfaces. The performers summon you into the woods, amplifying all manner of small and precious flora and fauna, to reveal a needed refuge. Re-Leaf Agency is a recruitment session disguised as a performance, or maybe it’s a performance disguised as a recruitment session. Either way, this is the last time in 2026 when you can join the Agency to become a keeper of the good. Three Re-Leaf Agents - two dancers and a recruitment officer - implore you to join them in navigating the turbulent times in which we find ourselves. Amidst the anxiety of an unraveling democracy and the impacts of a changing climate, Re-Leaf Agency rekindles hope by taking the long view of the natural world. This multimedia piece is the culmination of several years documenting a sliver of earth on the edge of Maryland’s South Mountain, during which time MAD Dance director Kit Clark experienced the solace of non-human time while walking and witnessing the land. Re-Leaf Agency shares that profound experience with others. Dancers Amanda Comi and Jeanna Riscigno join Clark in this one-of-a-kind performance.

record.title: SILENT FILM Series: A Fool There Was (1915)
record.description: Kiss Me, My Fool! Seductive, scandalous, and groundbreaking for its time, A Fool There Was introduced audiences to one of the first great screen icons: Theda Bara, the original “vamp.” Bara stars as a mysterious temptress whose charm and manipulation lead respectable men toward obsession and ruin. Exploring themes of desire, morality, and destructive passion, the film shocked audiences upon its release and helped establish the image of the femme fatale that would influence generations of Hollywood storytelling. Bara’s performance remains mesmerizing more than a century later, making this landmark film a fascinating glimpse into the origins of cinematic stardom. record.title: SILENT FILM Series: Battleship Potemkin (1925)
record.description: A Pulse-pounding Story of Rebellion, Courage & Action Battleship Potemkin is widely regarded as one of the most influential films in cinema history. This landmark silent film dramatizes the 1905 mutiny aboard the Russian battleship Potemkin , transforming a historical event into a powerful story of resistance, justice, and collective action. Renowned for its groundbreaking editing techniques, the film’s iconic “Odessa Steps” sequence remains one of the most studied and celebrated scenes ever captured on screen. Featuring a cast of largely non-professional actors, Battleship Potemkin helped revolutionize filmmaking through Eisenstein’s innovative use of montage . Nearly a century after its release, the film continues to inspire audiences and filmmakers worldwide, earning its place among the greatest motion pictures ever made. record.title: Special Film Event: The Lion’s Roar
record.description: A Tribute to the Memory, Dignity & Legacy of Frederick County’s African American History The Lion’s Roar is a powerful documentary honoring the voices, memories, and lived experiences of Frederick County’s African American elders. Through intimate interviews with local “Living Treasures,” the film preserves stories of childhood, family, faith, work, education, segregation, resilience, and community life across generations. From memories of Lincoln High School and one-room schoolhouses to stories of Black-owned businesses, home births, domestic work, military service, church life, neighborhood traditions, and the everyday strength required to live through Jim Crow, The Lion’s Roar gives audiences a rare opportunity to hear history told by the people who lived it. At its heart, this documentary is a tribute to these elders, who do more than recall the past—they remind us how love, discipline, perseverance, humor, and community helped shape Frederick’s Black history and continue to shape its future. African American Resources Cultural and Heritage Society (AARCH Society) website . This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s Special Film Events , celebrating filmmaking and on-screen storytelling. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop for a memorable film experience.

record.title: Sweet Dreams: Mandy Barnett Sings Patsy Cline
record.description: “Sweet Dreams” is a stunning tribute to the timeless music of Patsy Cline. The concert features a collection of iconic classic country songs originally recorded by Patsy Cline, including “Crazy,” “Sweet Dreams,” “Walking After Midnight,” “I Fall to Pieces,” “Always,” “Faded Love,” “She’s Got You,” “Strange,” and many more. Widely considered Nashville’s finest vocalist, Mandy Barnett rose to prominence at the age of 18 after being chosen among 400 auditionees by the legendary Ryman Auditorium for the title role in the 1994 musical production of Always… Patsy Cline . Her successful performance as Patsy Cline garnered tremendous press, both domestic and international, establishing the production as a staple of American theater. An official member of the Grand Ole Opry since 2021, Mandy has performed on more than 400 occasions, sharing the stage with legendary performers including Dolly Parton, Ringo Starr, Kristin Chenoweth, Pat Benatar, Judy Collins, Connie Stevens, Garth Brooks, and Michael Feinstein, among numerous others. record.title: U.S. Army Band: Pershing’s Own
record.description: For over 100 years, the U.S. Army “Pershing’s Own” Concert Band has provided the soundtrack to history in Washington, D.C., as the premier musical organization of the nation’s senior service. Join us for an engaging evening of symphonic blockbusters, music from the stage and silver screen, and patriotic favorites. The U.S. Army Band “Pershing’s Own” was formed on January 25, 1922, by order of General John J. Pershing. General Pershing believed that bands played a vital role in troop morale and efficiency and was convinced that America needed a premier band to surpass those of Europe. “Pershing’s Own” provides musical support for the leadership of the United States, to include all branches of government, and to a wide spectrum of national and international events to connect the Army to the American people. record.title: Well Being Concert: Cathy Fink and Marcy Marxer with Chao Tian – From China to Appalachia
record.description: A Cross-Cultural Celebration of Music and Friendship The second of our Well Being Concerts in partnership with Carnegie Hall Weill Music Institute , this event reimagines live performance as a source of comfort, connection, and mental restoration, highlighting the arts’ role in health and wellness, and the need for non-clinical mental health support. Grammy Award-winning American Roots artists Cathy Fink and Marcy Marxer join Chinese classical hammered dulcimer player Chao Tian in a show that combines music from China, Appalachia, and beyond. Instrumentation includes the yangqin (Chinese hammered dulcimer), gourd banjo, five-string banjo, ukulele, guitars, dumbek, cello-banjo, and mandolin. Songs are performed in both English and Chinese. From China to Appalachia was born from a friendship and a mutual love of musical exploration experienced through jam sessions that inspired a show highlighting the power of music to connect cultures. The group has performed together since 2017 and has toured extensively since 2023. The band’s first album, From China to Appalachia , reached No. 1 on the Folk Music radio charts and No. 3 on Billboard ’s Bluegrass Charts. This show is part of New Spire Arts’ programming . New Spire Stages , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers an intimate venue for a memorable concert experience.

record.title: Adrian Dunn and the Adrian Dunn Singers (Platinum)
record.description: Composer, conductor, and visionary artist Adrian Dunn brings his genre-defying sound to the stage with the Adrian Dunn Singers. Known for their precision, emotional depth, and electrifying presence, the Adrian Dunn Singers transform the concert hall into a space of both reverence and urgency. record.title: BCPA Presents: A Christmas Carol
record.venue: Bowie Center for the Performing Arts
record.description: Early Bird pricing available until October 10! Celebrate the holidays at the Bowie Center for the Performing Arts with our acclaimed production of Charles Dickens’ A CHRISTMAS CAROL, adapted and directed by Christopher Dwyer. Filled with music, magic, humor, and heart, this heartwarming holiday favorite brings the beloved story to life for audiences of all ages! Dickens’ timeless tale follows Ebenezer Scrooge on an extraordinary journey of redemption. Visited by his former business partner, Jacob Marley, and three mysterious spirits, Scrooge is forced to confront his past, reconsider his present, and peer into his future to discover the importance of family, generosity, empathy — and the true spirit of the holiday season. Returning for its fourth annual season, with a few surprising updates, the BCPA’s own A CHRISTMAS CAROL features a cast of professional actors and musicians performing alongside talented community performers of all ages! Join us to celebrate the season, connect as a community, and support your friends and neighbors performing on the BCPA mainstage. This performance is supported in part by the Maryland State Arts Council ( msac.org ) and The City of Bowie .

record.title: Beyond the 4th: Stories of Laurel’s FreedomCelebrations
record.description: Beyond the 4th: Stories of Laurel’s Freedom Celebrations explores how Laurel has celebrated independence and freedom, from the 1876 Centennial to the 1976 Bicentennial and beyond. Through artifacts, photographs, and personal stories, we invite you to discover how Laurel has come together to honor freedom and community. record.description: GYPASO Productions, in partnership with SMADO Films, proudly announces the Red Carpet Film Premiere of “Give Your Parents A Standing Ovation,” returning by popular demand for a special engagement at the Bowie Center for the Performing Arts. The premiere will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with doors opening at 6:00 PM and the film beginning at 7:00 PM. This highly anticipated event invites families, caregivers, seniors, and community members to celebrate a story that uplifts, heals, and honors the people who raised us. “Give Your Parents A Standing Ovation” is a tender, intergenerational story that reminds us of the beauty, complexity, and responsibility of loving our elders. Through themes of aging, gratitude, forgiveness, and reconnection, the film encourages viewers to pause, reflect, and honor the people who shaped their lives. Brought to life by director Bruce Odams and writer/producer/co-director Dr. Gybrilla Ballard Blakes, the film weaves heartfelt storytelling with real-world impact. Their collaboration creates a moving cinematic experience that resonates with families, caregivers, and communities everywhere.

record.title: We Call the Earth Our Mother: Stories of Thanks with Dovie Thomason
record.description: This performance takes place on, Tuesday, November 17, 2026. When registering there are TWO time slots. Please visit the link for more information. This performance is part of our Education on Stage/Field Trip Series and is recommended for children in PreK-Grade 5. Renowned storyteller and cultural educator Dovie Thomason presents a special on-stage educational performance celebrating Native American Heritage Month. As we prepare for Thanksgiving, Stories of Thanks shares the tales of many cultures explaining the original “whys” of the world, as science does now. The imagery and values in the stories from Dovie’s Native ancestry pair the “whys” of science with the very contemporary “hows” of living in balance on our shared Earth. This enriching experience supports learning through the arts while inspiring students to listen deeply, celebrate heritage, and appreciate the power of stories passed down through generations.

record.title: 23rd Annual Yuri Gorbachev Exhibition
record.description: The Byrne Gallery announces its 31st anniversary this year with a celebration and exhibition of vivid oil and enamel paintings of internationally acclaimed artist Yuri Gorbachev. The Byrne Gallery welcomes Yuri Gorbachev for his 23rd annual exhibition in Middleburg, Virginia. The Gallery will feature some of his classic paintings along with new works from his 2026 museum tour. In 2026, he showed at venues in Talin Estonia, Helsinki Finland, Prague Czech Republic, and Berlin Germany as well as Gallery Chang in New York City and Seoul, Korea. The opening reception will be on November 14, 2026 from 5:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. The exhibition is open to the public and everyone is cordially invited to attend. The exhibition begins on November 4th and continues through January 3rd, 2027. This year a portion of the sales from the exhibition will be donated to the families of Ukraine through The International Rescue Committee (IRC) for Ukrainian Refugees. This organization is consistently awarded top marks by charity watchdog groups for efficient use of contributions and overall impact.

record.description: The Sprout 5K supports Sprout Therapeutic Riding & Education Center in Aldie, Virginia—a nonprofit (501(c)(3)) dedicated to changing lives through partnerships with horses. record.title: Birding Sweet Run
record.description: Sweet Run State Park has 894 acres of diverse habitat consisting of rich oak-hickory forest, meadows, ponds, streams, and vernal pools in northwestern Loudoun. It borders the Appalachian Trail and is only a couple of miles from the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers. Sweet Run is a wonderful sanctuary for Loudoun wildlife, with numerous bird species utilizing its richness. These walks are sponsored by Loudoun Wildlife Conservancy; bring binoculars if you have them. Sweet Run is located just north of Neersville at 11661 Harpers Ferry Road (Rte. 671); detailed directions at https://www.dcr.virginia.gov/state-parks/sweet-run. Registration required: Sign Up Online. Questions: Contact Joe Coleman at jcoleman@loudounwildlife.org. Parking fee: The fee for a standard vehicle is $10. View fee information at https://www.dcr.virginia.gov/state-parks/parking-fees. record.title: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep  Holiday Experience
record.description: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep Holiday Experience One of Scarlet Springs Farm’s most beloved holiday traditions is back! Cocoa, Cookies & Cows invites you to spend a festive afternoon with our adorable Highland cows, calves, Valais sheep, and lambs before warming up with homemade hot cocoa and cookies in our beautifully decorated Ridgetop Stable. Your experience begins with a 30-minute group animal immersion, where you’ll have the chance to pet, brush, feed, and love on our friendly Highland cows and calves, along with our famously puppy-dog-friendly Valais sheep and lambs. While the animals don’t mind sharing their barn, this portion of the experience will be largely outdoors, so please dress accordingly. After enjoying the highlands & lambs, we’ll clean up and then head down to the Ridgetop Stable, where you can warm up in our heated, enclosed space for the remaining hour while taking in the sweeping views of the farm. For the holidays, the stable will be transformed with festive décor and music to create the perfect cozy holiday setting. Settle in with your family, sip on homemade hot cocoa, enjoy a tower of delicious cookies, and soak up what makes Scarlet Springs so special. Before you head home, be sure to stop by The Scarlet Shop for Highland-inspired Christmas gifts and keepsakes. Whether this is your first visit or an annual family tradition, Cocoa, Cookies & Cows is the perfect way to slow down, get cozy, and make holiday memories together.​ ​What’s Included with Your Ticket: 1.5 hour experience on the beautiful 74-acre Scarlet Springs Far 30 minutes with the Highlands — pet, brush, feed, and meet our fluffy, friendly Highland cows and calves Time with our Valais sheep and lambs Seat with your party in our festive, beautifully decorated and heated Ridgetop Stable Homemade hot cocoa and cookies Sweeping views of the farm and a festive holiday atmosphere

record.title: Environmental Film Night - Water’s Way: Thinking Like a Watershed
record.venue: The Hill School's Sheila C. Johnson Performing Art Center
record.description: Step into the hidden history of the Chesapeake Bay watershed through Water’s Way: Thinking Like a Watershed, produced by The Bay Journal. Once shaped by millions of beaver ponds and natural wetlands, this landscape was designed to slow, spread, and filter water as it moved through creeks and rivers toward the Bay. Over time, development, agriculture, and the channelization of streams have disrupted these natural systems leaving behind what scientists call an “ecological amnesia” about how watersheds once functioned. Through compelling storytelling and stunning visuals, Water’s Way explores how natural elements like beavers, trees, and restored wetlands could help repair these processes and improve water quality once again. Before and after the screening, converse with local conservation professionals about watershed health and practical ways communities can support restoration efforts close to home. Light refreshments will be served. This event is free and open to the public, but registration is encouraged. Donations are graciously accepted. Doors open at 5:30pm | Movie 6:15pm

Conceived by founder and guitarist Craig Locicero alongside his creative brother, drummer Chris Kontos, the foundational energy of bassist Matt Camacho, the versatility and poise of guitarist Jeremy Von Epp, and Skinner’s voracious fresh approach, Forbidden sees the band arriving at their finest hour with their richest-ever line-up. With Skinner stepping up to take on lyrical duties, Forbidden takes a fierce and uncompromising look into the eyes of our times without taking sides, instead imploring people to recognize the false conflicts created by the current society and how they can conquer and rise above them. Take the blistering roar of “Single Point Failure”, the beautiful orchestral savagery of “Flower of Life”, and the relentless charge of “Burning The Lungs Of Earth.” There’s also the mid-paced brooding power of “Psyclops,” the twisting, winding power force of “Sycophantasy” featuring guest vocals from Mastodon’s Brann Dailor, and a thunderous ode to women “The Burden” featuring guest vocals from Kayla Dixon. record.title: Gaelic Storm
record.description: It’s hard to imagine a band just coming into their own after 20 years of success, but that’s exactly what makes a true anomaly. Gaelic Storm, a multi-national, Celticjuggernaut grows stronger with each live performance, and after two decades and over 2000 shows, they are a true force to be reckoned with. The band attributes their continued success to their fanatic audience, and it’s a well-diversified crowd for sure – attracting fans of every genre with their richstorytelling, energetic instrumentals, devotion to Celtic traditions and passion for their stagecraft. They are as loyal to their fans as the fans are to them, as frontman Patrick Murphy states, “The fans are the ones that have given us this life. We’re here for them.” Gaelic Storm takes a true blue-collar, hard-nose approach to touring, consistently traveling the US and internationally forging a unique path in the Celtic musicworld. “You have to see us live. We are the true working-man’s’ band,” says longtime member Ryan Lacey. “We still, and most likely always will, tour most of theyear, and that’s how we constantly hone our craft.” This dedication to their live show dates all the way back to the mid-1990s, when Gaelic Storm kicked off its’ career as a pub band in Santa Monica, California. Onewhich performance led to their discovery that ultimately found the band appearing in the blockbuster film, Titanic (where they performed “Irish Party in ThirdClass”). This laid the groundwork for a career that would eventually find them topping the Billboard World Chart six times, making appearances at mainstreammusic festivals, and regularly headlining the largest Irish Festivals across the country, all while gaining a reputation as a genre-bending Irish rock band whosesongs mix Celtic traditions with something uniquely creative. Recent years have seen the addition of Natalya Kay on fiddle and Parker Hastings on guitar, who both bring their own energy, musicianship and spirit to GaelicStorm.

record.description: High Tea with the Highlands: A Bridgerton-Inspired Tea Party + Highland Cow + Lamb Affair ​ ​Dearest Gentle Readers, It would appear that the ladies of Scarlet Springs Farm have once again orchestrated an affair most enchanting. If you enjoy the Bridgerton series, this is an outing you most certainly won't want to miss as you are most cordially invited to step into a world of romance, refinement, and a touch of pastoral intrigue.​ This two-hour group experience begins, as all great stories should, with an introduction to the true nobility of the countryside—our beloved Highland cows , each most appropriately named after the illustrious Bridgerton family. Spend 30 delightful minutes meeting, petting, brushing, and doting on Penelope and Eloise, tending to Hyacinth and Daphne, and positively swooning over the ever-dashing Benedict. And lest one think the excitement ends there, Simon, Colin, and Alfie—accompanied by their charming entourage of Valais Blacknose and Babydoll lambs—shall also be awaiting your acquaintance, eagerly accepting cuddles, treats, and no small measure of admiration. ​Following your audience with the Highlands, guests will gather for a proper full tea service , thoughtfully prepared and styled for an elegant yet whimsical afternoon. Expect a locally-sourced loose-leaf hot tea accompanied by a classic tea fare prix-fix menu with items such as: Radish and butter tea sandwiches Deviled egg Carrot salad sandwiches Chicken salad tea sandwiches Cucumber tea sandwiches Turkey with cranberry tea sandwiches Fall-flavored scones served with clotted cream and jam Buttermilk biscuits A variety of sweet treats, fit for the ton. (Exact selections may vary by chef.)​ Perfectly suited for couples, a girls’ day out, or a charming mommy & me experience, High Tea with the Highlands promises laughter, indulgence, and memories worthy of society’s highest praise. One can only assume tickets will be in great demand. Yours most sincerely, Lady Whistledown​ ​ $99 per adu

record.title: Loudoun Pours to Explore
record.description: Hosted by the Loudoun Wineries and Winegrowers Association, this new tasting series is an intimate, elevated wine experience designed for guests who want to taste with intention and learn from the region’s best producers. Each event features a thoughtfully selected group of Loudoun wineries pouring a focused selection of vinifera-based wines showcasing the stylistic range and growing sophistication of the county’s winegrowing landscape. A respected sommelier will guide the evening with an opening introduction, offering context around Loudoun’s terroir, grape varieties, and winemaking philosophies, while remaining available throughout the event for guest engagement. The experience is complemented by live music and an abundant grazing board of artisanal cheeses, charcuterie, and seasonal accompaniments, creating a refined yet relaxed atmosphere. This tasting series is intentionally positioned as an educational wine gala, not a festival. record.title: Magic on The Mountain
record.description: Join October One Vineyard at Walsh Family Wine for Magic on the Mountain on November 21st for a collaborative evening celebrating a stellar collection of vineyards on the Blue Ridge. CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE YOUR TICKETS – $155 before taxes For those who haven’t experienced Magic on the Mountain before, this annual event brings together four vineyards planted along the Blue Ridge Mountains in Bluemont: Lost Creek Vineyard, Bluemont Vineyard, October One Vineyard, and Walsh Family Wine. Together, these producers are beginning to emerge as distinct voices of the upcoming Bluemont AVA. Hosted at Walsh Family Wine, the evening features a seminar-style tasting showcasing all four producers, with wines thoughtfully paired alongside a dinner from Chef Katie Rowley of Wined and Dined. Part seated tasting, part celebratory dinner, this is a one-of-a-kind opportunity to experience the wines, vineyards, and collaboration shaping this emerging Virginia wine region. $155 per person. 21+ only. Seating is limited to ensure a comfortable environment. Please arrive promptly at 6:30 p.m. to enjoy the full experience. *PLEASE NOTE: This event is being held @ Walsh Family Wine 16031 Hillsboro Road, Purcellville, VA 20132

record.title: Nomini Bay Oyster Festival
record.description: The folks of Nomini Bay Oysters will be on the mountain all weekend serving their famous Virginia grown oysters! Enjoy them raw and grilled, with specialty options and the classics, that pair perfectly with Dirt Farm beer. Nomini Bay will be set up outside so dress appropriately and get ready for a beautiful day in the fresh mountain air! *No reservations needed. From Nomini Bay Oyster Ranch: "Nomini Bay Oyster Ranch began operations in 2014, but our love of the Bay and oysters spans over 50 years. Co-owned by Paul Simpson, Todd Neilson and Jess Jones, the mission of Nomini Bay Oyster Ranch is simple… Protect the Bay by farming oysters. Sell Virginia-grown oysters that are always fresh and taste great. Support our community through partnerships and service. A portion of all sales help clean the Chesapeake Bay."

record.title: Nooks & Crannies
record.description: Step off the well-worn path and into the hidden heart of the Davis Mansion on our Nooks & Crannies Specialty Tour. This behind-the-scenes experience invites you to slip past closed doors and into rarely seen rooms that most visitors never get to explore. Led by Jana Shafagoj, Morven Park’s Director of Preservation & History, you’ll uncover fascinating details, architectural surprises, and stories that bring the mansion’s past vividly to life. It’s no wonder this is our most popular specialty tour—spaces are limited and tickets sell out quickly. The 60-minute guided tour is capped at just 12 guests, making it an intimate and engaging experience, and is recommended for ages 12 and up.

record.title: November Gratitude Hike
record.description: November is National Gratitude Month and there’s no better place to practice mindfulness than the pristine forest. Hike 1-2 meandering miles with an experienced trail guide and Virginia Master Naturalist to take in the sights & sounds of nature in Autumn! As we hike, we’ll follow a self-made scavenger hunt to discover all we’re grateful for in nature! MEET at the Visitor Center.REGISTER for free at https://bit.ly/BansheePrograms.

record.title: November Storytime Gone Wild & Nature Walk - Turkeys
record.description: There’s never been a storytime like this! Explore nature stories and wildlife topics with a Virginia Master Naturalist each month through interactive and hands-on play. Weather permitting, storytime takes place outdoors under the trees every 4th Tuesday of the month. After storytime, we’ll embark on an easy walk in the woods connected to the seasonal stories we share – from bird watching and animal tracking to leaf identification and more! MEET at the Visitor's Center. In the event of rain, meet in the Education Complex. REGISTER for free at https://bit.ly/BansheePrograms. AGES 0-6 focus but all are welcome!

record.title: Paint Your pet at O1V
record.description: Join us at October One Vineyard on December 13 at 1:00 PM for a fun and creative afternoon with HueArt Works ! Artist Debbie will guide you step-by-step as you paint a one-of-a-kind portrait of your beloved pet. No painting experience is necessary! Your pet's photo will be transferred onto the canvas to provide a stencil and guide, allowing you to focus on adding your own artistic flair while Debbie walks you through the painting process. Before the Event After purchasing your ticket, please email a clear photo of your pet to hueartworksmd@gmail.com . Photos must be received by December 6th to allow time for your pet's image to be prepared for the event. Tickets are $55 and include all painting supplies, a canvas, step-by-step instruction from Debbie, and a flight of three (3) wines from the October One Vineyard tasting menu. record.title: Petals & Poses
record.description: Petals & Poses Join us for a cozy morning of stretch, wine, and flower arranging as we celebrate the fall season at Petals and Poses! Help us celebrate the season of gathering and friendship at the winery with a relaxing morning of yoga, floral arranging, and wine! Awaken your senses, calm your mind, and reconnect with your body and your community in this soul-nourishing event. Start the morning with a beginner-friendly yoga practice led by local pro Rhonda Wilson in our historic heartstone barn — focusing on breath, body awareness, and gentle movement to release tension, build strength, and constructive rest. Throughout this stretch to release focused practice, you’ll be prompted to participate in “let go” and allow your inner artist blossom. Please bring a yoga mat and a blanket, arrive by 9:45 AM, and layer up for comfort. Warm socks, a blanket, and water are also recommended! After yoga, dive into a hands-on floral arranging workshop with Angela Rabena of Blooms2u. You’ll create a sweet seasonal bouquet using fresh flowers in a reusable mason jar — no experience needed & all supplies included! Finally, relax and unwind at Kalero Vineyard with your favorite glass of wine — red, white, or rosé. Your first glass is included in your ticket. Sales end Saturday 11/14 at 7pm — don’t wait! Grab your friends & treat yourself to a morning of movement, creativity, and connection.

record.title: Revolutionary Stories: Indigenous Americans and the American Revolution
record.description: James “Jay” G. Harrison III, Executive Director of The Museum of Culpeper History, historian, first person living history interpreter, and archaeologist will discuss the history of Indigenous Americans in the American Revolution. In particular, he will examine the alliances of Native nations: how they viewed the war, why some tribes remained neutral, why others chose the side of the American colonists and while still others allied themselves with the British. In addition, Mr. Harrison will discuss the roles and contributions of Indigenous Americans during this conflict as diplomats, scouts and soldiers. Event Details: Sunday, November 8, 2026 Program begins at 2:00 p.m. RSVP Required Revolutionary Stories is open to the public, and presentations will be uploaded to our YouTube channel. Check out Loudoun Museum’s social media, website, and sign up for our newsletter to find out about program announcements, updates, and more. The program series are made possible in part by a grant from Virginia Humanities.

record.title: Saint Cecelia Harvest Wine Dinner and Ball
record.description: In the years before a national Thanksgiving Day friends and neighbors would gather for a harvest dinner, giving thanks for the blessings of the year and for the promise of the dawning of the next. These dinners always included social dancing such as the Virginia Reel. Because these celebrations occurred in November they became associated with Saint Cecelia, who in some liturgical calendars was identified as the patron of music. At Shiloh Manor Farm we continue this old Virginia tradition! We are partnering with Magnolias at the Mill to present a tradition Saint Cecelia dinner inspired by a 200 year old book on Virginia cooking authored by one of Patrick Henry’s granddaughters. Following dinner musicians from the Greater Washington Folklore Society will perform traditional English Country Dance tunes that were well known in colonial Virginia such as the Virginia Reel. Dan Gillespie, a highly respected historical dance master will be on hand to teach and call the dances. No experience needed! Comfortable clothing and shoes are a must but we encourage formal or historic attire. A prize will be awarded for best costume!

record.title: A Tribute to John Lodge - An Evening of Moody Blues Magic
record.description: John Lodge was the legendary bass player, songwriter, and vocalist of Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees The Moody Blues. As the songwriter of mega Moody Blues hits including “Ride My See-Saw,” “I’m Just A Singer (In A Rock and Roll Band),” “Isn’t Life Strange,” and more, Lodge performed and recorded with The Moody Blues for more than five decades, selling in excess of 70 million albums worldwide. Following his sad passing in October last year, his son-in-law Jon Davison (of YES), long-term collaborator Alan Hewitt (keyboards for The Moody Blues band), and his daughter Emily came together to create a unique concert to honor John, his life, and the iconic music of The Moody Blues - with the goal to touch hearts, spread happiness, and celebrate what John always described as “the soundtrack of his life.” The premiere in July captured a rare magic by seamlessly weaving archival vocals and footage of John into a live set performed by the musicians who had been by his side for the last ten years. Earning both rave critical reviews and ecstatic fan acclaim, this breathtaking technical feat created an incredibly powerful, spiritual atmosphere where it was as if John were performing in perfect harmony with his band. Attendees described it as having “amazing sound, lights, and live performances,” and calling it “a masterstroke, very emotional & unforgettable.” Continuing in how John's tours honored all of his bandmates, Jon Davison will bring his beautiful, soaring vocals to legendary songs such as "Nights in White Satin" and "Tuesday Afternoon." The show also includes tributes to Ray Thomas and Mike Pinder, together with the stunning video of Graeme Edge reciting "Late Lament" - which he originally recorded for John so that he could always be on stage beside him. John always wanted audiences to leave his shows with joy in their hearts - and that is exactly what this show delivers. The performance features a curated setlist that explodes with massive hits and deep-cut fan fav

record.title: A Virtual Lecture from Historic Annapolis – Exotic Imports & Elegant Dining: Annapolis in Its Golden Age (1763–1774)
record.description: Step into the world of colonial luxury with food historian Joyce White in this engaging lecture exploring the remarkable imported foods that defined status and refinement in Annapolis during the 1700s. This convergence of wealth and robust trade, particularly during the city’s Golden Age, allowed the wealthiest residents access to an extraordinary array of global delicacies—spices, sugars, teas, coffees, chocolate, fine wines, spirits, cheeses, and more—each reflecting far-reaching trade networks and cultural exchange. Discover how these coveted ingredients shaped fashionable dining and learn about Maryland’s skilled culinary artisans—many of them enslaved people—whose expertise transformed imported luxuries into elegant meals. The lecture concludes with a fascinating look at festive traditions documented in Maryland during this vibrant and prosperous era. Join us for a richly illustrated journey into the tastes, tables, and traditions of colonial Annapolis. record.title: A Virtual Lecture from Historic Annapolis – William and Dinah Nuthead: Maryland’s First Printers
record.description: Before Jonas and Anne Catharine Hoof Green, there was William and Dinah Nuthead, Maryland’s first printing duo. William Nuthead was the first printer in Maryland and the first to operate a press in Virginia, establishing his business in St. Mary’s City in 1685 after being barred from printing in Virginia by the colonial government. Following his death in 1695, his widow Dinah Nuthead took over the business and became the first licensed female printer in the American colonies. Join Rod Cofield as he discusses his research into their lives that led to his Maryland Historical Magazine article, “Much Ado about Nuthead.” The Historic Annapolis Virtual Lecture Series is offered free of charge thanks to the generosity of an anonymous donor. record.title: African American Heritage Tour
record.description: Trace the journey of notable Marylanders and explore their impact both nationally and internationally. This two-hour walking tour, offered in partnership with the Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Foundation and named a “Heritage Award Winner” by the Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area, starts at Market House Park across from Annapolis City Dock, where slave ships entered 300 years ago. The Alex Haley statue that marks the significance of the author of Roots and the journey of his ancestor Kunta Kinte is featured. Symbolically, the stroll continues uphill through local history to the State House and the statue of Thurgood Marshall, the first African American Supreme Court Justice. Hear of famous Marylanders, such as Harriet Tubman and Frederick Douglass. Your period-attired guide will highlight the importance of the Underground Railroad in the Chesapeake Bay region. During colonial times, the labor of both the enslaved and free blacks was the cornerstone upon which the tobacco economy was built. In the 19th century, Maryland was home to more free African Americans than any other state. Presently, Maryland continues to grow because of the important contributions made by her African American residents. The Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Foundation receives 20% of the proceeds.

record.description: America’s 250 Private Cruise Celebrate on the Water Aboard Darling Put on your red, white, and blue and join us aboard our beautifully restored 1973 classic yacht for the perfect way to honor America’s 250th birthday! record.title: Annapolis Witches & Legends Walking Tour
record.description: Take a walk through the history of Maryland's witch trials, superstition, and local legends with Annapolis Ghost Tours. Between the 1600s and 1700s, Maryland saw at least twelve witch trials. The last one was a capital case held right here in Annapolis. Several women in the colony were killed under suspicion of witchcraft, one was legally executed, and the stories of others have become legends that persist to this day. On this 90-minute walking tour, we will talk about the superstitions and accusations through the lens of local history.

record.title: Atlanta Rhythm Section
record.description: The Atlanta Rhythm Section… ARS… In the annals of rock and roll, where do they fit? They put out 15 albums of excellent original material and consistently put on entertaining live shows-both of which helped establish a broad if not huge fan base. They had some big hits and have been a major player in the Southern Rock scene. But is that the whole story? In some circles, maybe. But for those who’ve really gotten to know their music over the years, there’s a lot more to the story. ARS was paired with contemporaries Lynyrd Skynyrd as the successors to the Allman Brothers – carrying the mantle of “Southern Rock” in the late 70s. Based in Atlanta, Georgia, it may have made sense at the time. But performing songs that were more musically diverse and having hits that had a softer, pop sound, the “Southern Rock” label was a mixed blessing and many of their unique musical accomplishments became lost in a genre that has lived on to this day-but never really fit ARS. They've been part of the Southern Rock scene for over 50 years. Their biggest hits include So Into You, Champagne Jam, Imaginary Lover, Homesick, and Spooky. But there's so much more ... With 15 albums of outstanding songwriting and performances, The Atlanta Rhythm Section represents the good things the phrase "classic rock" implies.

record.title: AudaTours Naval Academy Audio Tour: Legends & Landmarks of Anne Arundel Unveiled

With this immersive self-guided audio tour, wind through Annapolis and beyond to unearth daring escapes, forbidden rituals, and echoes of forgotten ambition. Let local legends and scandalous moments reveal themselves just out of sight. What secret pact brought midnight mayhem to the Herndon Monument’s base? Who risked reputation and safety to spark a clandestine protest beneath the Naval Academy Chapel’s soaring dome? And why does an unmarked grave behind St. Anne’s Church bear no name, only whispers? Move through shadows and sunlight. Every step draws you closer to another crossroads, a new revelation, a rush of drama beneath quiet facades. Uncover the hidden pulse of Annapolis. Your discovery begins now.

record.title: Capitol Fools
record.description: What happens when Washington, D.C.’s premiere, political satire group - The Capitol Steps - call it quits after nearly 40 years? Most folks would agree that it was a great run, and the story would end there. But an intrepid group of cast members and a co-writer would not go quietly into that good night. This band of fools reflected on a world without musical, political satire, and didn’t like what they saw. And just like that The Capitol Fools were born. While foolish enough to embark on this new journey, they were smart enough to not reinvent the wheel. Fast-paced, laugh out loud show…check. Equal opportunity offenders…check. Skewering both sides of the aisle…check. If a “Steps-style show” is wrong, they don’t want to be right. The Capitol Fools hold up a mirror to our crazy political culture, providing hilarious song parodies and foolish reflections that inspire belly-laughter as both sides of the aisle get skewered. Cast members from past seasons of the Capitol Steps perform all the beloved bits, the mind-boggling backward talking spoonerisms, break-neck costume changes, over-the-top impressions, and song parodies reflecting the day’s news. The spirit, irreverence and D.N.A. of The Capitol Steps lives on with The Capitol Fools!

record.title: Carbon Leaf
record.description: Carbon Leaf’s fifteenth studio album, Time is the Playground is both a call to action and an embrace of the moment. Marrying nostalgic storytelling to nuanced, folk-infused indie rock, the Richmond, Virginia band embroiders heartfelt melody and harmony with acoustic and electric instrumentation to create a 12-song rumination on time, love and personal growth that’s equal parts urgent epiphany and contented exhalation. Originally formed as a college cover band in 1992 and with over 3,500 famously enthused live shows together, Carbon Leaf helped to define the aughts indie rock that they ultimately outgrew and outlasted. They first earned national recognition with “The Boxer,” a song that won the American Music Awards 2002 New Music Award and made Carbon Leaf the first unsigned band to perform before millions on the AMAs.

record.title: Chesapeake Sunrise Photographic Experience
record.address: Pier 4 Marina, 301 Fourth Street, Annapolis, MD 21403
record.description: A Luxury On-the-Water Photographic Workshop We are pleased to partner with acclaimed photographer Jeff Poe to offer refined, on-the-water photographic workshop experiences. This creative partnership combines the elegance of a Darling Charter with a hands on photographic learning experiences (for amateurs to seasoned photographers). Step aboard Darling at first light. As your captain navigates to the region's most compelling sunrise locations, Jeff provides continuous guidance to help you capture exceptional images in a truly unique setting. This intimate workshop emphasizes: Understanding light and composition Unlocking hidden photo features on phones and optimizing camera settings Photographing iconic landmarks such as Thomas Point Lighthouse and the Chesapeake Bay Bridge Capturing local wildlife, including ospreys and great blue herons. What's included on your private Photographic Workshop Cruise: 3.5 hours on the water aboard Darling for your group (up to 6 guests) USCG certified captain Hands-on photographic instruction by Jeff Poe throughout the experience Freshly baked scones, coffee & assortment of cold beverages Complete Package Price: $1,950 (for up to 6 guests) More details on our website, or contact us to learn more. Note : We are also doing a few public workshops where you can purchase individual tickets. See our website for these limited dates.
record.categories: Arts & Culture, On the Water, Outdoors, America 250

record.title: Christmas in the Capital: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees
record.description: Welcome the holidays with Watermark's Christmas in the Capital Tour: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees. Meet your period-attired guide inside our cozy office before embarking on your tour. Stroll with your colonial guide around Maryland’s capital city, trimmed in greenery for the season. Hear holiday traditions of times past and present as you walk by colonial mansions, Victorian homes, and quaint shops A highlight of the tour is the Maryland State House, with decorated Christmas trees representing the different counties of Maryland, presented by the Federated Garden Clubs of Maryland. The tour ends at Annapolis's grand Christmas tree at Market House Park. Take home the holiday cheer with a goody bag of treats including George Washington’s famed eggnog recipe!

record.title: Christmas Traditions by Candlelight at the William Paca House
record.description: Gather your family and friends and experience the joy of the holiday season with a festive tour of the William Paca House! On this guided candlelit tour, explore holiday traditions that have evolved over time and discover how families in Annapolis and Maryland celebrated the holiday season in generations past. Learn how the Paca household prepared to welcome friends and guests for the holidays. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a sweet treat, and a take-home recipe to help bring a taste of the past to your own holiday celebrations. record.title: Classic Theatre of Maryland presents: SCHOOL FOR WIVES
record.description: An Enchanting Summer Evening of Comedy Under the Stars! Spend a magical summer evening in the historic courtyard of Reynolds Tavern with Molière's sparkling comedy of romance, wit, and mistaken intentions. Set against the charm and beauty of one of Annapolis' most treasured landmarks, The School for Wives brings classic theatre to life in an unforgettable outdoor experience. Follow the hilariously overconfident Arnolphe as his carefully crafted plans for love begin to unravel, leading to a delightful whirlwind of deception, laughter, and unexpected surprises. Filled with clever wordplay, lively characters, and timeless humor, this beloved comedy proves that love has a way of defying even the best-laid plans. Running throughout the summer season in the beautiful outdoor courtyard at Reynolds Tavern, The School for Wives is the perfect way to enjoy an evening of professional theatre, historic charm, and unforgettable entertainment under the stars.

record.title: Clay Aiken: Rewind 2027 Tour
record.description: America first fell in love with Clay Aiken's extraordinary voice and undeniable charisma on the second season of American Idol. His journey on the show became a cultural phenomenon, drawing nearly 40 million viewers to the finale—one of the highest-rated live television broadcasts of the 21st century—and launching one of the most successful recording careers to emerge from the series. Aiken's first single, “This Is The Night,” made history as the first track by a brand-new artist to enter the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 1, selling nearly 400,000 copies in its opening week. The follow-up, “Invisible,” became a defining early-2000s pop hit, climbing to No. 37 on the Hot 100 and earning RIAA Gold certification. His debut album, Measure of a Man, then entered the Billboard 200 at No. 1 and went multi-platinum, cementing him as one of pop music's biggest new artists. Among his early highlights was the chart-topping holiday album Merry Christmas with Love, which still holds the record for the largest debut week ever for a holiday album in the SoundScan era. During the first seven years of his recording career, Aiken sold more than six million albums worldwide while becoming a fixture on television and one of the most successful touring artists to emerge from the early 2000s pop era. His rich tenor voice, emotional delivery, and ability to effortlessly move between contemporary pop, adult contemporary, inspirational music, and timeless standards have earned him a loyal, multi-generational audience. Aiken’s career has extended well beyond the recording studio, including a Broadway run in Monty Python’s Spamalot and a reunion with Ruben Studdard in 2018 for Ruben & Clay’s First Annual Christmas Carol Family Fun Pageant Spectacular Reunion Show, which The New York Times hailed as “a Christmas miracle.” The pair reunited once again in 2023 for a tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of their landmark American Idol season before competing together on Fox’s The Masked Singer in 202

Stroll by modest homes and gentry mansions as you learn about the many people who have made Annapolis what it is today.

record.title: Coppélia
record.description: Join the Ballet Theatre of Maryland for whimsy and humor in a tale of love and mistaken identity! Originally staged in 1870, Coppélia follows the comedic foibles of the feisty village girl, Swanhilda. When the local toymaker, Dr. Coppélius, creates a doll so true-to-life that everyone mistakes her for a real girl, it causes a stir in Swanhilda’s village. Franz, Swanhilda’s boyfriend, is particularly hoodwinked. Jealous of his attentions to this “girl with the enamel eyes”, Swanhilda sneaks into Dr. Coppélius’s workshop only to discover the truth: Franz has fallen in love with a doll! No sooner does Swanhilda realize this when Dr. Coppélius returns. There’s nowhere to run or hide, so she does the only logical thing: she puts on the doll’s clothes and pretends it has come to life. Swanhilda must keep her wits about her if she wants to make it out of the workshop with the toymaker none the wiser! Audiences will be charmed by Coppélia’s lively characters, whimsical humor, and joyful dancing. This playful narrative brings the perfect end to Ballet Theatre of Maryland’s 48th season.

As they tapped into their infinite fascination with that strange duality, singer/guitarist John McCauley, guitarist/singer Ian O’Neil, drummer/singer Dennis Ryan, and bassist Christopher Ryan assembled a batch of songs exploring desperation, grief, redemption, and resilience with both cinematic detail and lived-in emotionality. A sharp new turn from one of indie-rock’s most enduringly vital forces, Coin-O-Matic arrives as a complicated love letter to a way of life slowly slipping from the collective memory.

record.title: Eddie 9V
record.description: Eddie 9V’s 2024 album Saratoga was a breakthrough — a raw, road-ready blend of Southern soul, blues, rock, and funk that helped launch the Georgia-born artist from cult favorite to national spotlight. Since its release, his monthly Spotify listeners have grown from 8,000 to peaking at over 800,000, driven by standout tracks like “Halo,” “Saratoga,” and “Love Moves Slow,” all now certified on SiriusXM’s Spectrum channel. Now signed to Dan Auerbach’s Easy Eye Sound, Eddie is gearing up for a brand-new album in 2026. With national tours, radio airplay, and a band firing on all cylinders, he’s proving that gritty, honest music still cuts through — and his best songs may still be ahead.

record.title: Emmaline: Sinatra, My Sweetheart Tour
record.description: Following nearly two consecutive years of completely sold-out headlining performances, jazz-pop vocalist, violinist, and songwriter Emmaline announces the Sinatra, My Sweetheart Tour, reimagining Frank Sinatra's timeless classics with vintage romance and a modern feminine twist. Featuring selections from her upcoming album “Sinatra, My Sweetheart,” this nostalgic performance blends lush arrangements, virtuosic violin, and Emmaline's signature modern-retro style into an evening that feels both nostalgic and refreshingly new. Though still in the early stages of her blossoming career, vocalist, violinist and songwriter, Emmaline, has accomplished an impressive laundry list of achievements so far. From being featured in top music publications such as Rolling Stone and American Songwriter to performing as the opening act for GRAMMY winning icons Chaka Khan and Kenny G and being named “Best Vocal Jazz of 2023” by Spotify, this Nashville-based independent artist captivates the hearts of all who hear her smoky, jazz-infused, genre-fluid voice. As one of the leading independent female songwriters and arrangers of her generation, Emmaline has garnered tens of millions of streams with her independently released EPs All My Sweetest Dreams, Necessity, Retro Kind of Love and Indiana Skies. In November of 2025, she released her long-awaited Christmas Album, which experienced immediate virality, gaining over 5 million streams within the first week of release and charting at #34 on the jazz radio charts.

record.title: End of The Line : An Allman Brothers Tribute
record.description: End Of The Line is the premiere Allman Brothers tribute band. Having carved up the southeast with sold out shows in Georgia & Tennessee, End Of The Line is making a name for themselves with a sound as classic & heavy as the original Brothers themselves. From the authentic, raspy vocal approach of Justin Smith to the chugging drum/percussion train of Chase Bader & Ryan McClanahan, the band both pays homage while pushing the boundaries of the timeless & extensive catalog. Carrying the electric weight of Duane Allman is Conor Kelly & his counterpart Dickey is Adam Gorman, who is the band's lone Maconite. Last, but certainly not least, the low end duties are vastly covered by Casey Conway, who is a perfect bottom end sandwich of Berry, Allen, and Oteil. With endorsements from the official Allman Brothers Museum, The Big House, End Of The Line carries on the legacy of The Allman Brothers with poise & power. Come experience the soul, the guitarmony, the jam, and the ramblin' spirit that still lives on through each note hit.

record.title: Falco & Book (Of The Infamous Stringdusters) Play Jerry Garcia
record.description: Andy Falco and Travis Book are both members of the Grammy award winning bluegrass band The Infamous Stringdusters. Inspired by their love of the music of Jerry Garcia, the duo branches off on their own for occasional tours to celebrate Garcia’s timeless songs. “The project actually originated back stage at ‘Dusters shows where Travis and I would typically warm up with some fun Jerry songs” Falco explains. “At some point we just thought it would be fun to do it in public” They draw from Garcia’s solo material, his Grateful Dead catalogue as well as the Traditional songs Jerry loved to play. “Performing this music as a duo allows us to explore the songs and jam in a way that’s unique to playing as a Duo” Says Book. “We typically hear these songs in larger ensembles, but the songs done with just bass and guitar somehow make the music very interactive with the audience. It’s really a testament to the quality of the songwriting, and we like to put a spotlight on that aspect of Jerry.”
