record.title: Food Glorious Food: Class, Culture and Cooking in Colonial Annapolis
record.description: Step back in time and explore the tastes, traditions, and stories that shaped colonial Annapolis! This immersive walking tour reveals how food reflected class, culture, trade, and daily life. Visit three distinctive historic sites: the Waterfront Warehouse, Hogshead Trades Museum, and William Paca House & Garden. Along the way, discover how global trade, local ingredients, social status, and enslavement shaped what Annapolitans ate and how food was prepared and served. Explore the everyday foodways of working and middling residents, the elaborate dining customs of the city’s elite, and the essential labor and culinary knowledge of enslaved people. Enjoy period-inspired tastes and sensory experiences along the way while discovering Annapolis’s past through its kitchens, markets, and tables! Advance registration required; space is limited. Recommended for ages 13+ This event will also be offered at 2:00 pm . Cost: General Admission: $20. Children (13-17), HA Members and Military: $15. The cost includes the Paca Garden admission. Program notes: Please wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather, as the tour is held rain or shine. The tour route is approximately ¼ miles long and includes elevation changes and uneven walking surfaces. Starts: Waterfront Watehouse 4 Pinkney Street Annapolis MD 20401 Ends: William Paca House & Garden 186 Prince George Street Annapolis, MD 20401 Food Allergy Notice: Food samples will be provided at this program. record.title: Forces of Nature with violinist Francesca Anderegg
record.venue: Maryland Hall for the Creative Arts
record.description: ANNAPOLIS SYMPHONY ORCHESTRA FORCES OF NATURE Friday, November 6, 2026 Saturday, November 7, 2026 6:30 PM Pre Concert Lecture 7:30 PM Concert At Maryland Hall MUSIC PROGRAM Luke Soneral An Overture: The Mouse and its Shadow Reinaldo Moya Vestido de Mar, with violinist Francesca Anderegg Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky The Tempest, Op. 18 Igor Stravinsky Divertimento from Le baiser de la fée (The Fairy’s Kiss) This concert is approximately 2 hours in length, with a 20 minute intermission. In Forces of Nature, the natural world becomes a source of wonder, reflection, and transformation. Emerging composer Luke Soneral opens the program with An Overture: The Mouse and Its Shadow, offering an exciting glimpse of orchestral music’s future. Reinaldo Moya’s ocean-inspired violin concerto, Vestido de Mar, brings violinist Francesca Anderegg to the stage for a work that reflects the landscapes and experiences of the Americas. Tchaikovsky’s The Tempest turns Shakespeare’s storm into a powerful exploration of human nature, while Stravinsky’s The Fairy’s Kiss honors Tchaikovsky through the wintry world of Hans Christian Andersen. Together, these works reveal nature as both an elemental force and a mirror of our inner lives.

record.title: G. Love & Special Sauce - Yeah, It’s That Easy 30th Anniversary Tour w/ Todd Carey
record.description: G. Love & Special Sauce is an American Hip-Hop Blues band known for its unique fusion of hip-hop, blues, funk, and soul. Formed in 1993 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, the band originally featured Garrett Dutton, aka G. Love, as the lead vocalist and guitarist, Jeffrey Clemens on drums, and Jim Prescott on bass. The trio quickly gained attention for their laid-back, groovy style and G. Love’s unique vocal delivery, blending rap-like spoken word with bluesy singing. Their debut self-titled album, G. Love & Special Sauce, was released in 1994 on Epic Records and included the hit single “Cold Beverage,” which became popular on alternative radio stations and MTV, solidifying their presence in the music scene. The band’s style has been described as a mix of “slacker blues” and “alternative hip-hop,” as they frequently incorporate elements of 90s hip-hop beats with classic blues rhythms. Over the years, G. Love & Special Sauce has released numerous albums, including Coast to Coast Motel (1995), Yeah, It’s That Easy (1997), The Electric Mile (2001) and the GRAMMY nominated The Juice (2020). Their sound evolved to include more soul, R&B, and rock influences, though they retained their laid-back vibe and clever lyrical play. Their 2014 album Sugar saw a reunion of the original lineup after several years, and they continued to tour and produce music with a loyal fan base. Known for their energetic live performances, G. Love & Special Sauce has played at festivals like Bonnaroo and Lollapalooza. Garrett Dutton also frequently collaborates with other artists, including Jack Johnson, with whom he shares a similar vibe, and has released solo projects that dive deeper into his blues influences. G. Love & Special Sauce remains a beloved name in the music scene, blending genres in a way that feels fresh and authentic.
record.categories: Nightlife, Arts & Culture, Concerts & Live Music

record.title: Gabe Dixon
record.description: Since Gabe Dixon first emerged in 1999, he has been penning honest and heartfelt songs that continue to garner fans and crowds across the globe. Gabe's songs have been covered by many; Garth Brooks, Taj Mahal, Keb Mo and Ben Rector to name a few. Gabe's music has also appeared in major films such as The Proposal and TV shows such as Nashville, Grey’s Anatomy, Vampire Diaries, and Parks & Recreation. Along with his own appearances on Jimmy Kimmel Live! and The Late Late Show, Dixon has performed and collaborated with notable acts like Paul McCartney, Alison Krauss & Union Station, Supertramp, Loggins & Messina, and O.A.R. In 2019, Gabe joined the Tedeschi Trucks Band as a full-time keyboardist and vocalist contributing significantly to the writing and recording of their their last 4-album tour-de-force, I Am The Moon. He and his trio were subsequently featured on the 36-show “Wheels Of Soul” tour alongside Tedeschi Trucks Band and Los Lobos. Recently, Gabe has continued to captivate listeners, releasing his full-length studio album, Parts I’ve Played, alongside multiple live and studio EPs, with another full-length record on the horizon.

record.title: Gaelic Storm
record.description: It’s hard to imagine a band just coming into their own after 20 years of success, but that’s exactly what makes a true anomaly. Gaelic Storm, a multi-national, Celtic juggernaut grows stronger with each live performance, and after two decades and over 2000 shows, they are a true force to be reckoned with. The band attributes their continued success to their fanatic audience, and it’s a well-diversified crowd for sure – attracting fans of every genre with their rich storytelling, energetic instrumentals, devotion to Celtic traditions and passion for their stagecraft. They are as loyal to their fans as the fans are to them, as front man Patrick Murphy states, “The fans are the ones that have given us this life. We’re here for them.”

record.title: Gary Gulman's 7th Hour: An All-New Standup Show
record.description: Over 30 years in comedy, Gary Gulman has established himself as an eminent performer and peerless writer. A product of Boston, Gulman has been a scholarship college football player, an accountant, and a high school teacher. He has made countless television appearances as both a comedian and an actor. Gulman has made five masterful TV specials including his most recent universally acclaimed stand-up specials for HBO Max, “Born On 3rd Base”, lending his meticulous comedic craft to the current Tale of Two Cities-esque wealth gap, and “The Great Depresh”, a tour de force look at mental illness, which is equal parts hilarious and inspiring. Most recently, Gary made his off-broadway debut with a 5 week sold out run at The Lucille Lortel Theatre of his critically acclaimed one man show "Grandiloquent" directed by Tony Award winner Moritz von Stuelpnagel and produced by Mike & Carlee Productions ("Oh Mary"). In 2019, he appeared in the international blockbuster “Joker”. He can most recently be seen co-starring with Amy Schumer in the hit Hulu comedy series, “Life & Beth”. Gary's first book published by Flatiron Books is titled “Misfit: Growing Up Awkward in the '80s”, a memoir based on his life from Kindergarten through Twelfth Grade. It was released in September of 2023. Amy Schumer called the book “laugh out loud funny and heartfelt” and MacArthur Fellowship recipient Adrian Nicole LeBlanc found it “exquisite, love-affirming and generous”.

record.title: Healthy Forests Workday: Invasive Plant Removal at Bacon Ridge Natural Area
record.address: 1801 Hawkins Road, Crownsville, MD, 21401, Crownsville, MD 21032
record.description: Protect the Health of YOUR Local Forest: Join us at Bacon Ridge Natural Area in Crownsville to spend a morning removing harmful invasive plants from along the trails! Scenic Rivers’ Healthy Forests Program engages community volunteers to help protect the long-term vitality of our largest conservation easement located within Bacon Ridge Natural Area. Our October 2026 workday will focus on vines, shrubs, and grasses. These aggressive invaders threaten vegetation at all levels of the forest from the ground up into the forest canopy. Event Details: Volunteers will be working on designated trail sections to remove specific invasive plant species. Volunteers will be trained in how to identify and remove these plants. Work gloves and tools can be provided by Scenic Rivers, though volunteers are welcome to bring their own gear. To participate, volunteers must: Be 16 years or older to attend without a supervising adult. Volunteers age 10 to 15 may attend with an accompanying adult(s) to supervise work; Be able to hike up to 1 mile to get to designated work areas. Wear long sleeve shirts, long pants, and closed toed shoes. Poison ivy is present in these work areas. Bring a full water bottle. We must have at least 5 registered volunteers for the workday to proceed. So, be sure to invite some friends! Controlling invasive species infestations is a big job and we’ll be happy to have as much help as possible!

record.title: Jesse Cook
record.description: A global artist in every sense of the word, Jesse Cook redefines music’s power to connect people across cultures and continents. Over the last three decades, the Paris-born, Toronto-raised master of the Spanish guitar has built a devoted following for his spellbinding rumba flamenco, routinely selling out performance halls from London to Los Angeles, Milan to Montreal. On stage, Cook radiates infectious energy, collaborating with his band and guest instrumentalists to craft immersive, unforgettable experiences. His concerts are celebrated for their warmth, precision, and emotional depth. Throughout his decades-long career, Jesse Cook has remained devoted to musical exploration. His boundary-defying artistry has introduced flamenco and world music to wider audiences while maintaining a signature style that is both technically masterful and soulfully expressive. That authenticity has clearly resonated—with over a billion streams and views across platforms to date—proving his sound remains as relevant as it is revered.

record.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. record.description: Celebrate the Holiday Season Through the Spirit of America 250 with Historic Annapolis! As America commemorates its 250th anniversary, step back to the holiday season of 1776 and experience Yuletide in Annapolis at the William Paca House & Garden and the Hogshead Trades Museum. Discover how early Americans celebrated the season through traditional music, engaging storytelling, and festive customs that brought families and communities together during the nation’s founding era. It’s a unique opportunity to experience the sights, sounds, and traditions of the season while reflecting on the history of our country’s beginnings. Your Yuletide admission includes access to both historic sites, and you may begin your journey at either location. record.title: Jon Lampley
record.description: What comes next after 11 years with The Late Show with Stephen Colbert’s house band? For Jon Lampley, the answer is Notes To Self — his sophomore solo album, out June 26, 2026, and a deeply personal statement from an artist stepping fully into the spotlight. With praise from NPR and The New York Times already behind him, Lampley enters this next chapter with confidence and clarity. Lampley has made his name as a consummate trumpet and sousaphone player, singer-songwriter, composer, and bandleader, blending jazz, soul, gospel, and contemporary roots music. On The Late Show, he performed nightly under bandleaders Louis Cato and Jon Batiste, honing his craft and stage presence before a global audience. Produced by Lampley, The Diner (Jordan Cohen, Clyde Lawrence, Jonny Koh), and Michael Thurber, Notes To Self pairs introspective songwriting with the virtuosity, joy, and communal energy that define his career. The album reflects on ambition, optimism, faith, and growth, with standout tracks like “Greener,” “JOY,” and “Maybe.” Beyond late-night television, Lampley has built a reputation as one of the most versatile brass players of his generation. He co-founded the high-energy jazz-funk ensemble Huntertones and has performed in amphitheaters, arenas, and festivals with jam-rock mainstays O.A.R. and pop-soul powerhouse Lake Street Dive. Long regarded as an elite collaborator and sideman, Lampley has increasingly stepped forward as a frontman, composer, and creative force in his own right. That instinct to lead is rooted in his upbringing in Akron, Ohio, where church music shaped both his sound and philosophy. Learning trumpet by ear and absorbing the emotional power of communal performance, Lampley developed a style centered on connection, intention, and atmosphere. He continued refining his craft at The Ohio State University before relocating to Brooklyn, New York, where his artistic vision fully crystallized. record.title: Last Train Home
record.description: For more than a quarter century, Last Train Home has been one of the most fun, creative, and adventurous bands you'll ever hear, blending rock and country and bluegrass with swing and sambas, Tin Pan Alley and indie, lush pop and barrelhouse blues. Since its debut recording in 1997 right up through its 2022 release Everything Will Be, Last Train Home has followed a path unlike any other. With members in Nashville, Washington D.C., and Bucks Co. PA, the band's live shows are more rare these days than they used to be, but the group continues to create music together. They worked through the pandemic on Everything Will Be, the stunning follow-up to 2020's stellar Daytime Highs and Overnight Lows release, each member in relative isolation sending their parts from their home studios for producer/mixer/wizard Jared Bartlett to wrangle into a cohesive whole. With the band's usual trademark horns, pedal steel, rich harmonies, and rhythmic invention, the record features seven originals by band leader Eric Brace, plus four deftly chosen covers. Critics have found lots to like with Everything Will Be: "Brace and Last Train Home continue to be one of roots music's most enduring and inventive bands. This album proves it." – Country Standard Time

record.title: Life of Courage: Bruce McCandless and the Pacific War
record.venue: U.S. Naval Institute's Jack C. Taylor Conference Center
record.description: Join the U.S. Naval Institute on 10 November 2026 at 10:30 AM ET at the Jack C. Taylor Conference Center, in Annapolis, MD for a look inside the new book Iron and Fire: The Pacific War Story of Destroyer Captain Bruce McCandless with Bruce McCandless III as he recounts his grandfather’s—Admiral Bruce McCandless—wartime experiences across the Pacific. Lieutenant Bruce McCandless was at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, fought aboard the heavy cruiser USS San Francisco (CA 38) through the brutal Guadalcanal campaign. Later promoted to captain, he commanded the destroyer USS Gregory (DD 802) during the final drive across the Pacific. Late in life, retiring as an admiral, he dictated his wartime memories to his daughter Sue; the manuscript was then set aside for many years. Iron and Fire draws on family letters, photographs, shipmates’ recollections, and stories passed down through generations to share his story. Registration and other Information: All in-person guests must register by 25 September 2026. Due to the requirements of the U.S. Naval Academy and the timing of this event, in person attendance is only open to U.S. citizens. The conference will take place at the U.S. Naval Institute's Jack C. Taylor Conference Center, which is located on the grounds of the U.S. Naval Academy. A limited amount of parking is available at the Jack C. Taylor Conference Center. We welcome our audience in-person and via live-stream on the U.S. Naval Institute’s YouTube Channel.

record.title: Lonesome River Band
record.description: It’s hard to think of a genre more committed to sustained creative careers than bluegrass. Case in point: the 41-years-and-counting path of Mountain Home Music Company stalwarts, Lonesome River Band. Though the last remaining original member departed before the turn of the century, the group — a quintet for more than 20 years now — hasn’t so much reinvented itself as refined a profoundly influential signature sound that has a seemingly endless appeal to successive generations of fans and musicians alike. Led by 30-plus year veteran and award-winning banjo man Sammy Shelor, who has presided over one stellar lineup after another, LRB remains among the genre’s most widely admired and powerful draws, both in person and on streaming platforms.
record.categories: Nightlife, Arts & Culture, Concerts & Live Music

record.title: Marc Roberge of O.A.R.
record.description: As frontman for multi-platinum-selling rock band O.A.R., Marc Roberge has performed for sold-out crowds at some of the world’s most iconic venues while helping build a remarkably devoted global fanbase. Three decades into O.A.R.’s career, the New York City-based singer/songwriter/guitarist has also developed a distinct identity as a solo performer. Roberge’s solo shows trade the full-band energy of O.A.R. for an intimate, stripped-back setting, featuring reimagined O.A.R. favorites, select covers and candid conversation with the audience. The format puts a spotlight on the deeply personal storytelling that has been central to his songwriting since O.A.R.’s formation in 1996. Inspired in part by the tradition of classic country and folk troubadours, Roberge continues to explore the more lyrical and roots-oriented side of his songwriting through his solo work.
record.categories: Nightlife, Arts & Culture, Concerts & Live Music

record.title: Marshall Crenshaw Band w. Sarah Borges
record.description: Born in 1953 in Detroit, Michigan, Marshall Crenshaw learned to tune a guitar correctly at age ten and has been trying ever since. His first big break came in 1978 playing John Lennon in “Beatlemania”, first as an understudy in New York, then in the West Coast company, followed by a national touring company. Removing himself from that situation in Feb. 1980, Marshall settled in New York City. Enthralled by the hyper-diverse musical culture of the City, and the local Rock scene in particular, Marshall formed a Rock and Roll band with brother Robert on drums and Chris Donato on bass. Of his City Winery New York show last fall Infocus Visions Music & Arts Magazine hailed, “Marshall Crenshaw live is an experience in itself. Forget the solo artist; this is a full band explosion that showcases the magic of musical synergy. Watching them on stage is like peeking into a creative engine room. You see the interplay, the energy flowing between them, how each member feeds off the others to create that signature Marshall Crenshaw sound.”

record.title: Maryland Witches Pub Crawl
record.description: The Witches of Maryland Pub Crawl is a tour through the history of witch trials, accusations, superstitions, and legends. Sip on a beverage while entertained by stories of suspicion, fear, and the women whose names were tied to witchcraft in Annapolis and across Maryland. Your guide will bring to life the legends, trials, and lore that shaped our colonial past. The Witches of Maryland Pub Crawl is a 2-hour pub crawl (approx. ½ mile) into some of the storied taverns of Annapolis. Spending about 20–30 minutes at each location, you’ll relax with a cocktail while learning about the accusations, trials, and superstitions that spread through Maryland — and the lasting stories that have become part of our local history. We will visit three bars on each crawl — locations visited may include some of the following: 🍸 Drinks are not included in this tour. This tour is limited to Adults (21+) ONLY! No children. show less

record.title: Matthew Morrison: Show Up
record.description: Matthew Morrison is a versatile actor who is recognized for his work on-stage and on-screen. He has been nominated for Tony, Emmy and Golden Globe Awards. Morrison made his debut on Broadway in “Footloose” but his big break came when he was cast as heartthrob Link Larkin in the hit “Hairspray.” Morrison was later nominated for a Tony Award for his role in “The Light in the Piazza,” and received a Drama Desk Nomination for Outstanding Actor in a Musical for “10 Million Miles.” He also starred in the Tony-winning revival of “South Pacific” at Lincoln Center Theater in New York. He also starred as “J.M Barrie” in the musical “Finding Neverland.” Morrison received two Drama Desk nominations for his role, and won the category of Favorite Actor in a Musical in the Broadway.com Audience Awards. In addition to his Broadway tenure Morrison is probably best known for starring in Fox’s musical comedy series “Glee,” where he played the director of the glee club, “Mr. Schuester.” The show was created by Ryan Murphy and received the Golden Globe award “Best Television Series – Comedy or Musical” in 2010 and 2011. Morrison was also nominated for Best Actor those years. Morrison has many other iconic roles on TV/Film, but most notably on the hit CBS show The Good Wife, where he played the role of U.S. Attorney, Conor Fox, through the series finale, and as Paul Stadler throughout Season 13 and 14 of ABC’s Grey’s Anatomy. Morrison has released four studio albums. His debut, self-titled album through Mercury Records in 2011, which featured an A-list lineup of guest artists including Sting, Gwyneth Paltrow and Sir Elton John. And most recently, “Where It All Began,” which is a Broadway standards record that was produced by the legendary Phil Ramone.

record.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
record.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
record.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

record.title: Mike Tramp of White Lion (Solo Acoustic)
record.description: Mike Tramp, legendary White Lion singer, songwriter and front man stepped out on his own in 1995 and began his 29-year long solo career. With twelve consistent solo albums to his name, you can easily say that he has stood his ground. Tramp has never steered off his path and is charging forward with confidence, and no desire to look back. Tramp says, "It really just meant that I knew who I wanted to be and sound like when I recorded my first solo album twenty-five years ago. Yet, one thing led to another, and as they say, you shouldn't let sleeping lions sleep for too long." Therefore, after much request to bring the White Lion songs back to the live circuit, Mike Tramp re-recorded 12 of White Lion's greatest hits, and also gave it a natural facelift, since it had been close to 40 years since the songs were originally written and recorded. The album, titled "Mike Tramp - Songs of White Lion" was released in April 2023 to rave reviews, with many saying how fresh and today the songs sounded. Some even said it sounded like a brand new album. The album brought Mike Tramp's White Lion around the world and included two tours of the USA in 2023. One thing led to another, and this August, "Songs Of White Lion Vol. II" will hit the streets followed by a two month tour across the USA with Mike Tramp's White Lion. Tramp says "White Lion was a chapter and a journey I was on; it was a one-way ticket with no return. The hair trend of the decade has since faded, but the music lives on, stronger than ever. He states, "It's both challenging and a joy for me. Still, the truth is that people don't know that most of these big rock songs started out as folk songs in a Brooklyn, NY basement."Which is the true secret to why they still work on stage. You can't keepа good song down.

record.title: Morgan James
record.description: Morgan James has a voice that needs to be heard; even when she was just a fifth grader belting out standards on a karaoke machine. After her grandmother heard her sing, the matriarch footed the bill for James’ voice lessons, positive that her granddaughter had the mysterious “it factor”. And, despite the sometimes treacherous terrain of the music industry, James has never tired in her quest. Whether it’s tussling with label executives, covering and owning songs by the likes of the Beatles or Prince, or creating her own brand of original soul music, James has carved out an enviable and diverse career, always on her own terms.

record.title: Paint From Your Soul Class
record.address: 1851 McGuckian Street, Suite B, Annapolis, MD 21401
record.description: Join us for a special 3-hour class of Paint From Your Soul, featuring The Healer archetype. This transformational art experience is designed for women to step away from daily stress, nurture themselves, and focus on healing our souls through creative expression. In this intimate, heart-centered session, we will explore the energy of The Healer to foster deep self-compassion, emotional restoration, and inner peace using art and personal symbolism. Through gentle breathwork, guided meditation, and an intuitive painting process, you will bypass the inner critic and let an expressive portrait emerge on the canvas that reflects your unique journey toward restoration. record.title: Papa Lebas & Gumbo Ya Ya featuring Joe Krown and Corey Arceneaux
record.description: Papa Lebas & Gumbo Ya Ya makes their majickal return to the Rams Head On Stage to celebrate multiple album releases, beginning with the band’s debut album, Naptown to NOLA, which will be available for the first time on vinyl. In addition, three band members have recent albums: New Orleans piano master and Kenny Wayne Shepherd sideman Joe Krown’s Qualified, International Zydeco Ambassador Corey Arceneaux’s Accordion Man, and multi-reed instrumentalist Seth Kibel’s Clarinet Without a Net. But the celebrations don’t end there, as every Papa performance is a party. Led by songwriter, producer, guitarist & bassist Jeff Muller (aka Papa Lebas), the project is a New Orleans-inspired earthy gumbo of funk, R&B, jazz, blues, zydeco, Cajun, brass band, and more—and a love letter to the power of community. Papa Lebas & Gumbo Ya Ya was launched last year with the album Naptown to NOLA which features 63 performers from Louisiana and the DMV including such notable musicians as Ivan Neville, George Porter Jr., Bill Summers, Chubby Carrier, Tommy Malone, Ron Holloway, Tommy Lepson, Deacon John, Leroy Jones, and many more. Like last year’s show, this one will feature a high-powered band of all star performers at the top of their game bringing the songs from the albums, along with other New Orleans gems, to life. Joe Krown is making the trip up from New Orleans for the show, joining some of the DMV’s finest and favorite musicians: Louisiana native Corey Arceneaux, Rahsaan “Wordslave” Eldridge (Honest Lee Soul), Meg Murray (Songbird Collective, Cyphers Band), Doug Woolverton (Kenny Wayne Shepherd, Beginnings), Seth Kibel (Daryl Davis Band), Chris Watling (The Grandsons, King Soul), Noah Pierre, Matt Tebo (Shari Puorto Band), and perhaps a special guest or two. Come out, join the party, and let your spirit soar!

record.title: Peter Mayer: A Stars & Promises Christmas "This Town"
record.description: Guitarist, Vocalist and Songwriter Peter Mayer brings his acclaimed Christmas tour to the stage this holiday in “A Stars and Promises Christmas – “This Town.” Mayer is a frequent traveler in the musical world, sharing the stage with James Taylor, Paul McCartney, Don Henley, Paul Simon, Dave Matthews and many others. Many know him best for his 35 years as lead guitarist for Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band, and from his own career as a songwriter-performer which include: Warner Bros. Artist PM, the Peter Mayer Group, and his collaboration with his son Brendan Mayer. His own musical journey includes more than 20 albums, among them, four Christmas albums. This marks the ensemble’s 27th year captivating crowds nationally with a world class group of musicians that includes violin, woodwinds, bagpipes, electric and acoustic guitars, percussion, electric and acoustic bass, and the rich harmony of five voices all moving seamlessly through an array of styles: Celtic reels, folk songs, world music rhythms, classical carols, jazz and rock ‘n roll, along with a nod to the music of Jimmy Buffett. Mayer muses; “I love this season of the year, celebrating the timeless songs and traditions of Christmas from around the world. Our theme for this year, “This Town,” focuses on the places we call home. As we navigate a lightning paced world, spanning great distances, Christmas calls us back to the friends, family and places that have raised us. As in the humble beginnings of the first Christmas, “This Town” must be the place where Joy, Hope, Peace and the spirit of giving we sing of each Christmas begins. In that spirit of giving, each Stars & Promises performance will benefit a local food bank and/or charity in “This Town.”
record.categories: Nightlife, Arts & Culture, Concerts & Live Music, Winter Occasions

record.title: Pressing Strings
record.description: Hailing from Annapolis, Maryland, Pressing Strings is a powerhouse trio–led by guitarist and vocalist Jordan Sokel–has earned a loyal following with their genre bending blend of blues, rock, and folk, wrapped in soul-stirring storytelling and toe tapping grooves. Their music resonates with the emotional grit of blues, the laid back swagger of folk, and the urgency of modern rock. Whether delivering heartfelt ballads or energetic anthems, Pressing Strings weaves lyrical introspection and high-caliber musicianship that feels both fresh and familiar. Sokel’s smokey voice and intricate guitar work is complimented masterfully by a star rhythm section. Held down tightly by drummer Justin Kruger–an energetic and charismatic performer whose style mirrors his outside the box personality and unique approach to the instrument, along with bassist Nick Welker–a solid and stoic figure who picks melodic lines and chordal voicings that makes the trio sound full and lush. All three members sing, adding harmonies reminiscent of southern California in the 70’s. Together they push the limits of what a trio can do and provide an immersive, feel-good vibe that hits the audience’s heart as hard as it does the ears.

record.title: Puzzling Adventures Scavenger  Hunt
record.description: Consistently rated the best local scavenger hunt since 2016! Puzzling Adventures are a cross between a scavenger hunt, an adventure race, and an informative self-guided walking tour. record.title: Rachael & Vilray w/ Taylor Ashton
record.description: Since their formation in 2015, Brooklyn-based duo Rachael & Vilray have achieved a certain timeless quality with their singular take on traditional pop. Though rooted in the language of an earlier age, their songs transcend nostalgia with wit and a flair for the theatrical. On their third album West of Broadway, vocalist Rachael Price (also of Lake Street Dive) and guitarist/singer/songwriter Vilray evolve their music’s previous dreaminess to achieve a refreshing angularity built on left-of-center instrumentation (e.g., vibraphone and alto saxophone coasting above the moody strains of baritone sax and trombone). record.title: The Amish Outlaws
record.description: It is a little-known fact that most Amish practice a tradition similar to the Christian “Confirmation” and Jewish “Bar Mitzvah” called “Rumspringa” (literal translation: “running around”) in which Amish children at the age of 16 have an opportunity to live free of the strict Amish code of conduct before deciding if they want to come back and be baptized into the Amish church. Surprisingly, virtually all of the youths return. But sometimes they don’t. Four out of the original six members of The Amish Outlaws were born and raised in Lancaster, PA and had a strict Amish upbringing. No electricity from land lines, no alcohol, no musical instruments, but their spirits were too wild for the Amish lifestyle. Once they trampled in the Devil’s Playground, there was no turning back. In the years since Rumspringa, the members of the Amish Outlaws have become very well acclimated to the pleasures and vices of the modern world… music, most of all. Hip hop, rock, country, metal, disco, opera. There is no genre they do not touch upon. Thus, with a bold lust for life and a fire for music and performance that can only come from 16 years of repression, The Amish Outlaws were unleashed upon the world.

record.title: The Seldom Scene
record.description: Fifty-three years into a legendary career, much has changed about The Seldom Scene, starting with the venerable progressive bluegrass quintet’s various lineup iterations over time. But even as band members have stepped in and out of various roles, what’s most important is what hasn’t changed: an undeniable knack for blending both old and new music and traditions without sacrificing what makes either potent and durable. Their current iteration is a true blue lineup: guitarist mandolin player Lou Reid, bassist Ronnie Simpkins, banjoist and fiddler Ron Stewart, dobro player Fred Travers, and guitarist Clay Hess. Since they started up together in 1971, The Seldom Scene has dexterously performed original and traditional songs while presenting fiery and soulful reinterpretations of material by Merle Haggard, James Taylor, and more. The concept of bluegrass unshackling itself from a conservative, straight-ahead mindset seems like a given now, when some of its biggest stars fill stadiums and cross over with mainstream audiences, but the continued presence of the Scene acts as a reminder that it wasn’t always so. Even if their playing style feels more at home in intimate clubs, where the audience can feel their exuberance radiating from the stage, the Scene’s elastic relationship to genre established an important precedent that encouraged their contemporaries and allowed bluegrass bands to expand their repertoire in ways that laid the groundwork for today’s bluegrass boom. Long live The Seldom Scene.

Wyeth House & Studio. Discover a distinguished collection of nineteenth- and twentieth-century American art, housed in a renovated nineteenth-century mill with a dramatic steel and glass addition that overlooks the bucolic Brandywine River. In 1911, artist N.C. Wyeth used proceeds from his Treasure Island illustrations to buy 18 acres near Chadds Ford, Pennsylvania. Today, the preserved house and studio feature original props, a large mural, and period furnishings that offer a glimpse into Wyeth’s work and family life. record.description: Join your colonial-attired guide to learn the weird, wacky, and unusual history of Annapolis. Hear tales about the Russian sailor buried in the Annapolis National Cemetery, the historic “mobile homes” of Annapolis, the Confederate captain who kept fighting the Civil War long after the South surrendered and then built a home in Annapolis, the missing State House cornerstone … and so much more!
